articles.title: Summer transfer window 2026: The 20 biggest deals
articles.summary: From Enzo Fernandez to Maxence Lacroix, BBC Sport lists the 20 biggest transfers of the summer window.
articles.body:
Premier League clubs broke their all-time summer transfer record as spending reached £3.5bn - but the biggest deals of the transfer window stretch across the globe.

Transfer records, World Cup standouts and unexpected departures feature in the 20 most expensive deals this summer, based on initial fees as reported by the BBC.

=18. Jan Paul van Hecke - Brighton to Tottenham, £52m

Van Hecke is reunited with former Brighton manager Roberto de Zerbi after Tottenham paid £52m for the Netherlands defender.

He started 36 Premier League games last season and led top-flight centre-backs for pressured ball carries.

=18. Maxence Lacroix - Crystal Palace to Chelsea, £52m

Chelsea eventually agreed a £52m deal for Lacroix after negotiations with Palace stretched beyond the World Cup.

The centre-back arrives having helped Palace win the Conference League last season and made three appearances for France at the World Cup.

=18. Tijjani Reijnders - Manchester City to Al-Qadsiah, £52m

Netherlands midfielder Reijnders leaves Manchester City after one season in England, joining Brendan Rodgers at Saudi Pro League side Al-Qadsiah.

City recouped £52m for the 28-year-old, who registered six goals and seven assists in 47 appearances last term.

=16. Crysencio Summerville - West Ham to Al-Hilal, £55m

Summerville opted for a move to Saudi Arabia despite reported interest from Manchester United and Roma.

The winger scored seven goals and supplied five assists for relegated West Ham last season, before adding two goals and two assists for the Netherlands at the World Cup.

=16. Jeremy Jacquet - Rennes to Liverpool, £55m

Liverpool agreed Jacquet's move in January, with the France Under-21 defender recovering from a shoulder injury in time for the new season.

The 21-year-old joins a defence which is being reshaped under new manager Andoni Iraola.

15. Iliman Ndiaye - Everton to Manchester City, £60m

Everton winger Iliman Ndiaye was in talks with Tottenham before Manchester City stepped in with a deal that could rise to £65m.

A fan favourite on Merseyside, "Skiliman" scored 15 goals and provided four assists in 67 Premier League games for the Toffees.

14. Goncalo Ramos - Paris St-Germain to AC Milan, £60.2m

Ramos, 25, became Ruben Amorim's first signing as Milan manager and the club's record purchase.

The Portugal striker leaves PSG having scored 45 goals in 131 games in three seasons.

13. Rodri - Manchester City to Barcelona, £65m

Rodri leaves City as one of the defining players of their recent era, having been central to their control in midfield and build-up play.

The former Ballon d'Or winner and current Spain captain, 30, was also one of the Premier League's most reliable ball-progressors and passers, making his exit a huge tactical loss for City as well as a major sale.

12. Anthony Gordon - Newcastle to Barcelona, £69.3m

Gordon signed for Barcelona after a 17-goal season for Newcastle , including 10 in 12 Champions League appearances.

The England winger, 25, also registered a goal and three assists at the World Cup before completing his move to Spain.

11. Carlos Baleba - Brighton to Manchester United, £70m

Manchester United have turned to Baleba to add more power and ball-carrying ability to their midfield.

The 22-year-old joins from Brighton for £70m after establishing himself as one of the Seagulls' key midfielders.

=9. Savinho - Manchester City to Tottenham, £75m

Two seasons after arriving in Manchester, Savinho moved to Tottenham in a £75m deal.

The Brazilian made 53 appearances for City, scoring twice and providing 12 assists.

=9. Bruno Guimaraes - Newcastle to Arsenal, £75m

Guimaraes, 28, said he wanted a new challenge after leaving Newcastle for Premier League champions Arsenal on a four-year deal.

The Brazil midfielder scored nine league goals last season before finishing the World Cup with four assists in five matches.

8. Ayyoub Bouaddi - Lille to Manchester City, £81.4m

Aged 18, Bouaddi arrives at City as part of a major midfield rebuild following the departures of Rodri and Tijjani Reijnders.

The Morocco international cost an initial £81.4m, with a further £4.2m potentially due in add-ons.

7. Mateus Fernandes - West Ham to Tottenham, £85m

Tottenham broke their transfer record to sign Fernandes after only one season at West Ham.

The 21-year-old Portugal midfielder made 36 league appearances, scoring three goals and providing four assists, while also winning 54 tackles.

6. Sandro Tonali - Newcastle to Tottenham, £92.5m

Spurs soon broke that record to sign 26-year-old Tonali for an initial £92.5m, with add-ons potentially taking the deal to £100m.

The Italy midfielder said a conversation with fellow Italian and Spurs manager Roberto de Zerbi played a major part in convincing him to join.

5. Bradley Barcola - Paris St-Germain to Liverpool, £106m

Liverpool completed the signing of France forward Bradley Barcola from Paris St-Germain for a fee worth up to £123m.

Barcola joined PSG from Lyon in 2023 for a reported £38.5m and won three Ligue 1 titles, two Champions Leagues, the French Cup twice, the Uefa Super Cup and the Fifa Intercontinental Cup.

4. Yan Diomande - RB Leipzig to Real Madrid, £115.7m

Real Madrid signed Diomande after interest from Liverpool and Paris St-Germain, in a deal which could be worth £120m including add-ons.

The 19-year-old Ivory Coast winger was named Bundesliga young player of the season, having recorded 12 goals and eight assists, and impressed at the World Cup.

3. Elliot Anderson - Nottingham Forest to Manchester City, £116m

Manchester City broke their transfer record to sign Anderson shortly after the England midfielder returned from the World Cup.

The 23-year-old played in all 38 Premier League games for Forest last season and described City as "winners - the sort of team I want to be a part of".

He was briefly the most expensive British footballer in history, before being surpassed by...

2. Morgan Rogers - Aston Villa to Chelsea, £117m

England attacking midfielder Rogers joined Chelsea from Villa for £117m.

The 23-year-old joins Xabi Alonso's side on a six-year deal, having recorded 10 goals and six assists in 37 league appearances last season.

1. Enzo Fernandez - Chelsea to Manchester City, £125m

Argentina international Enzo Fernandez became the Premier League's biggest signing when he swapped Stamford Bridge for Etihad Stadium on transfer deadline day.

It made the 25-year-old the fifth-most expensive transfer of all time, alongside Alexander Isak's move from Newcastle to Liverpool last summer.

articles.title: Marc-Oliver Doue refuerza el centro del campo del Cádiz desde Castalia
articles.standfirst: El futbolista francés llega traspasado desde el equipo 'orellut' y firma hasta 2030
articles.summary: El futbolista francés llega traspasado desde el equipo 'orellut' y firma hasta 2030
articles.body: El Cádiz sigue conformando su plantilla y ha cerrado el fichaje de Marc-Oliver Doue, procedente del Castellón. El centrocampista francés llega mediante un traspaso y firma con el conjunto amarillo hasta junio de 2030. Al equipo orellut llegó hace un año y ha disputado 33 partidos oficiales con la camiseta albinegra. El futbolista francés anotó tres goles con el club castellonense y ya no jugó este lunes en Balaídos en la victoria ante el Celta Fortuna, pese a venir de jugar en la segunda jornada en el partido que el Castellón disputó ante el Sabadell y que finalizó con empate. Nacido en Burdeos en 2000, Doue se formó en las categorías inferiores del Girondins y posteriormente pasó por Zwole y Virton. En 2023 llegó al fútbol español para jugar en el Eldense y después militó en la Ponferradina antes de incorporarse al Castellón. El nuevo jugador cadista acumula 44 partidos y tres goles en LaLiga Hypermotion. Su llegada completa uno de los principales objetivos del Cádiz durante las últimas horas del mercado, que era reforzar un centro del campo al que también se ha incorporado Aimen Moueffek. Doue viaja ya hacia Cádiz y este miércoles se pondrá por primera vez a las órdenes de Albert Celades.

articles.title: Calero ya tiene a su nuevo ‘10’: Mikel Goti aterriza en Oviedo... y se va Ilic
articles.standfirst: La Real Sociedad cede al mediapunta de 24 años hasta final de temporada sin incluir una opción de compra
articles.summary: La Real Sociedad cede al mediapunta de 24 años hasta final de temporada sin incluir una opción de compra
articles.body: El Real Oviedo completa su frente ofensivo con Mikel Goti. El conjunto carbayón ha cerrado con la Real Sociedad la cesión del mediapunta de 24 años hasta final de temporada, sin opción de compra, para proporcionar a Julián Calero una nueva alternativa en los últimos metros. La dirección deportiva encabezada por David Fernández buscaba un futbolista capaz de desenvolverse por dentro y encontró en el jugador vasco la pieza para completar esa parcela. La operación tomó velocidad en las últimas horas del mercado. Goti pretendía inicialmente permanecer en la Real Sociedad para pelear por una oportunidad, pero la insistencia del Oviedo terminó inclinando la balanza hacia el Carlos Tartiere. El mediapunta todavía no había disfrutado de minutos esta temporada y encontrará en Segunda la continuidad que necesita para seguir avanzando en su carrera. El nuevo futbolista azul ya conoce la categoría. Durante la segunda mitad de la pasada campaña jugó cedido en el Córdoba de Iván Ania, donde participó en 16 encuentros, nueve como titular, y marcó un gol. Su llegada se suma a la de David Jiménez en un último día de mercado intenso para un Oviedo que termina de entregar a Calero las últimas piezas de su plantilla. Además, el Oviedo ha puesto fin a la etapa de Luka Ilic en el conjunto carbayón. La entidad azul comunicó al futbolista la resolución de su contrato, por lo que el centrocampista serbio deja de pertenecer oficialmente a la disciplina oviedista. La salida de Ilic era uno de los asuntos que la dirección deportiva tenía pendientes de resolver en la recta final del mercado. Finalmente, ambas partes separan sus caminos y el jugador queda desvinculado del Oviedo para afrontar un nuevo destino en su carrera profesional. El club despidió al futbolista agradeciéndole el trabajo realizado durante su etapa como azul y deseándole éxito en su futuro personal y profesional. Su marcha termina de despejar uno de los últimos frentes abiertos en la plantilla de Julián Calero tras una jornada final de mercado con varios movimientos en las oficinas del Carlos Tartiere.

articles.title: El Tenerife completa su plantilla con el extremo Gerard Valentín
articles.standfirst: El extremo catalán, de 33 años, llega a la isla con la carta de libertad por petición de Álvaro Cervera tras su experiencia en el Al-Wakrah catarí
articles.summary: El extremo catalán, de 33 años, llega a la isla con la carta de libertad por petición de Álvaro Cervera tras su experiencia en el Al-Wakrah catarí
articles.body: El Tenerife ha cerrado este martes un acuerdo para que Gerard Valentín sea el último pasajero del proyecto construido por el club blanquiazul en la temporada de su retorno a Segunda. El extremo catalán, de 33 años, aterriza en la isla con la carta de libertad, como una petición expresa de Álvaro Cervera, tras haber pasado el último curso en el Al-Wakrah catarí y con más de 250 partidos disputados en Segunda. El polivalente extremo se ha comprometido por una campaña, aunque su contrato también contempla una extensión por otra más de manera opcional. Formado en las categorías inferiores del Figueres, Girona o Sevilla, inició su trayectoria deportiva con el Olot de la extinta Segunda B y, en la 2014-15, formó parte del Nástic de Tarragona que ascendió a Segunda. Valentín defendió la camiseta del club catalán durante dos ejercicios hasta que, en 2017, fichó por el Deportivo. Con los gallegos debutó en Primera división y a mitad de la temporada 2018-19 se marchó cedido al Lugo. Su gran rendimiento en el Anxo Carro propició que los lucenses se hiciesen en propiedad con sus servicios en 2020. Su velocidad y desborde llamaron la atención del Huesca, que acometió su traspaso en enero de 2022. Allí se erigió en uno de los pilares del club ascenso, con el que disputó 121 partidos oficiales en cuatro temporadas en las que, además, aportó cuatro goles. En el verano de 2025, el atacante catalán emprendió su primera aventura internacional en el fútbol árabe, donde disputó 19 citas oficiales entre Liga y Copa. Valentín llega ahora al Tenerife dispuesto a poner toda su experiencia, desborde y polivalencia al servicio de los esquemas de Álvaro Cervera con el firme objetivo de convertirse en uno de los grandes animadores del Heliodoro Rodríguez López

articles.title: Matías Orozco llega al Castellón
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista colombiano llega cedido por el Brighton inglés
articles.summary: El centrocampista colombiano llega cedido por el Brighton inglés
articles.body: El Castellón y el Brighton & Hove Albion han alcanzado un acuerdo para la cesión de Matías Orozco, centrocampista que se incorpora a la disciplina albinegra hasta el 30 de junio de 2027. Orozco suele jugar como pivote, posición que ha dejado una vacante en el conjunto albinegro con el traspaso de Marc-Olivier Doué al Cádiz. Matías Orozco (01/12/2007, Barranquilla, Colombia) aterriza desde el Brighton, club de la Premier League que se hizo con los servicios del colombiano desde el Deportivo Cali de su país natal. En este mismo mercado, el conjunto de la Premier League ya aplicó esta fórmula con el Castellón al ceder a Rodrigo Rego tras ficharlo de la cantera del Benfica. Formado en el conjunto sudamericano, Orozco ha sido convocado en las inferiores de su selección nacional, en los equipos Sub-19 y Sub-21. A nivel de clubes, disputó el Torneo Clausura de la 24/25 y el Torneo Apertura de la 25/26 con el Deportivo Cali, sumando 28 encuentros y anotando dos goles. Con esta son 13 las incorporaciones confirmadas por el Castellón en la ventana estival.

articles.title: El último movimiento del Girona será Carles Pérez
articles.standfirst: El extremo catalán firmará con los blanquirrojos una vez rescinda con el Celta
articles.summary: El extremo catalán firmará con los blanquirrojos una vez rescinda con el Celta
articles.body: Pese a estar centrado en dar salida a Azzedine Ouanahi, lo que puede ser la venta más importante del verano, el Girona hará un movimiento de entrada en su plantilla para reforzar el ataque, concretamente la banda izquierda, con Carles Pérez. El extremo ya ha rescindido con el Celta el año que le queda de contrato y firmará con el Girona como agente libre... seguramente ya este miércoles. Carles Pérez inyectará experiencia y calidad a la plantilla dirigida por Quique Álvarez, que en los últimos días perdió a Minsu en esa posición después que el Rangers pagara la clausula de 10 millones por el coreano. El de Granollers jugó el curso pasado cedido en el Aris de Salónica de Grecia cedido por su club, el Celta, que lo fichó el verano del 2023 de la Roma por 5,2 M€ y lo cedió por primera vez el año posterior al Getafe. El jugador se formó en el fútbol base de la Damm, el Espanyol y, durante muchos años, en el del Barça. Con los azulgrana debutó con el primer equipo -13 partidos en total- hasta que acabó primero cedido en la Roma y después comprado por los italianos por 13 millones. El canterano del club se marcha traspasado al club de Primera división portuguesa a cambio de una cantidad simbólica con un porcentaje de los derechos del ariete todavía para el Girona. Dawda ha defendido los colores blanquirrojos durante 13 temporadas, con un paréntesis de un curso, el pasado, en el Cádiz en Segunda. Dawda ha jugado en el primer equipo seis encuentros en total en los que ha anotado un tanto. El internacional con Mauritania inicia así una nueva aventura en el intento de progresar como futbolista

articles.title: El internacional israelí Tay Abed, nuevo jugador del Valladolid
articles.standfirst: Llega cedido del Levante y los pucelanos se reservan una opción de compra
articles.summary: Llega cedido del Levante y los pucelanos se reservan una opción de compra
articles.body: Además de la llegada de Dani Martín, el último día del mercado de fichajes veraniego trajo otro movimiento de entrada en el Real Valladolid. El club pucelano también incorporó al extremo Tay Abed como movimiento final, ya que la no salida de Marcos André evitó más incorporaciones en la delantera que se habían tanteado como la del francés Kevin Monzialo. Abed, internacional absoluto con Israel, que también tiene la nacionalidad española, llega cedido también por el club granota. La entidad pucelana se reserva una opción de compra, aunque, tal y como ha podido saber MARCA, la cifra supondría un alto montante que parece complicado que el Real Valladolid pueda hacer frente en un futuro. De este modo, el extremo, que inició su carrera en las categorías inferiores del Hapoel Tel Aviv y pasó también por las del PSV Eindhoven, refuerza la banda del ataque del Pucela. Zurdo de pie, el israelí puede jugar en ambas bandas, aunque suele desempeñarse mejor en la derecha, a pierna cambiada, de forma habitual. El levantinista competirá por un puesto con Yeray y De Rooij, que han empezado la temporada como titulares para Fran Escribá, pero en un equipo que aún no ha conseguido ganar después de tres jornadas disputadas.

articles.title: Aeroporto de Florianópolis terá voo direto para Assunção, no Paraguai | G1
articles.standfirst: Rota internacional temporária será oferecida a partir de janeiro de 2027.
articles.summary: A Gol operará o voo Florianópolis Assunção entre janeiro e fevereiro de 2027, facilitando o acesso de turistas ao litoral catarinense sem a necessidade de conexões.
articles.body:
Avião no Aeroporto de Florianópolis — Foto: Ricardo Wolffenbuttel/Divulgação

O Aeroporto de Florianópolis terá uma nova rota internacional temporária a partir de 5 de janeiro de 2027. O voo direto para Assunção, no Paraguai, vai operar durante a temporada de verão.

Anunciada pela Gol, a linha busca aproximar os turistas paraguaios do litoral de Santa Catarina. As viagens estarão disponíveis até 14 de fevereiro, período pós-Carnaval (veja datas abaixo).

Segundo a concessionária Zurich Airport, que administra o aeroporto, atualmente nenhuma companhia realiza esse trajeto. O destino já foi oferecido anteriormente por uma empresa aérea paraguaia.

De acordo com a companhia, a conveniência de chegar a Florianópolis sem a necessidade de fazer uma conexão torna a rota um chamariz para que os paraguaios em jornada solo, entre amigos ou em família explorem, inclusive emviagens de curta duração.

Mateus Pongeluppi, vice-presidente comercial da Gol, explica que Florianópolis é um dos destinos mais procurados pelos clientes da América do Sul no verão.

“A nova ligação internacional da Gol entre Assunção e a capital catarinense representa um ganho relevante em rapidez e conveniência para os passageiros de ambas as cidades e municípios adjacentes, ampliando a conectividade, as opções turísticas e o intercâmbio cultural entre o Brasil e o Paraguai”, diz.

🛩️ Os voos entre Florianópolis (FLN) e Assunção (ASU) serão operados com as aeronaves Boeing 737 da Gol, com capacidade para até 186 passageiros. Os bilhetes já estão disponíveis.

articles.title: Chicago Bears offer floor and ceiling cases in Round 4 of Yahoo Fantasy Expert League draft
articles.summary: The Bears were a popular target in Round 4 of our Yahoo Fantasy Expert League draft, but for different reasons.
articles.body:
The Yahoo Fantasy crew completed a 12-person draft for their expert league on Tuesday , which provided plenty of highlights. Among the more memorable moments in the draft came in Round 4 when two analysts tapped into the same offense for very different reasons to help build out their squads.

Chris Allen was content with a floor pick, while Scott Pianowski chased ceiling. Both analysts were buying the Chicago Bears.

Allen opened up the round, and he went with a boring but dependable pick, which is usually Pianowski's jam .

"I'll go running back here, 'cause I'm seeing a lot of the value and the talent here start to drop off," Allen said, before taking Chicago's D'Andre Swift. "I think the running game for Chicago is being under-discussed during the offseason. It's been more about what's your take on Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III, Colston Loveland.

"We're still talking about an offense that's still gonna run the ball quite a bit, especially once they get in scoring position. So I'm gonna get the guy that's more than likely gonna carry the mail for that offense."

The fantasy community has spent the summer arguing about which Bears pass catcher gets fed, and while they debated, Swift has been overlooked (he's being drafted as the RB20 on Yahoo).

Pianowski "loved" the selection, calling it the "ultimate boring value pick," then decided to get spicy with his own Round 4 selection.

A few selections later, the analyst most associated with drafting dependable veterans surprised the room with his pick.

"Harmon, you think you know me," Pianowski said. "You think I'm all about boring value veterans and healthy players.

"I'm going totally off type here with a helium, buzzy guy who's been hurt all summer. Give me Luther Burden III."

Burden was sidelined for a big portion of August due to a groin injury. He recently returned to practice and has looked healthy , leaving hope he'll be ready to go for Week 1 in what should be a high-octane offense with a shaky defense — the perfect combination for fantasy points.

"Ben Johnson has talked about setting scoring records," Pianowski said. "They'll have to set a scoring record if they wanna get back to the playoffs again. Talk about pinball teams, talk about carnival teams — the Bears check that box."

Pianowski has long said don't go looking for injuries during draft season because they'll find you during the season, but he couldn't resist the upside Burden and the Bears offer.

"If Burden's healthy, he's a smash as my wide receiver three," Pianowski said.

"I don't know what is more shocking — the fact that Scott took the Twitter buzzy guy," Harmon said. "Or you take the guy who's, like, missed all of training camp? Well, I don't know, I don't know who you are anymore."

A few picks after Swift and Burden came off the board, Colston Loveland followed. Pianowski summed it up best when he simply said "I want pieces of this offense."

The Bears have four players ranked in the top 50 on Yahoo's consensus rankings and five in the top 100 overall.

Swift is a rare dead-zone back with a clear role on an offense expected to score, yet his draft cost remains reasonable, in part because of his teammates getting more hype. If Chicago's offense delivers on expectations, Swift will get the goal-line work no matter who's catching passes, especially with Kyle Monangai week-to-week with a knee injury .

The bet on Burden is that the groin injury won't linger and the receiver builds on his impressive rookie campaign, taking another step in Year 2.

We'll have more takeaways from the Yahoo Fantasy Expert League in the days to come. You can also watch the full draft on YouTube .

articles.title: Real Madrid lose control of former academy starlet’s future after big-money move to the Premier League
articles.summary: One of the most significant moves for Real Madrid on the deadline day of the summer transfer window, surprisingly, had nothing to do with a direct departure...
articles.body:
One of the most significant moves for Real Madrid on the deadline day of the summer transfer window, surprisingly, had nothing to do with a direct departure or arrival from the club.

Instead, it was the sale of Chema Andres who moved from Stuttgart to Brighton and Hove Albion in the Premier League for a big fee, part of which Real Madrid were entitled to as they held 50% of the player's rights.

The youngster, thus, became part of a historic transfer window for Real Madrid where the club made over €200 million from youth player sales, windfalls and other similar operations.

As reported by Diario AS , Chema's move from Serie A to the Premier League closed for a sum of €23 million last night, making it a costly operation for Brighton.

Owing 50% of his rights, Real Madrid pocketed €11.5 million straight from the transfer and will be pleased with that development. There is, however, a twist.

After taking home their handsome windfall, Real Madrid have forfeited all rights over the player. Not only do they no longer hold a percentage of his ownership but they also have no more buy-back clauses or any priority purchase option.

The connection between Chema and Real Madrid is thus severed for good, and Brighton now own 100% of the player with complete control over his future.

Real Madrid knew well in advance that they would lose control of the player once his move to England went through but chose not to act on it.

The Merengues had a buy-back option on the player and could have signed him back this summer as an intermediate step before releasing him to Brighton if they wished to retain control.

Their decision not to interfere in matters is an indication that they were prepared to lose control of his future, and is thus a completely planned decision.

After all, the scope for Chema to return to Real Madrid in the long run is near-zero. Nevertheless, the hope will be that he can continue to flourish and grow in England into the player he has always been hyped to be.

articles.title: Confirmed: Promising defender leaves Barcelona after five years for Royal Antwerp in a €3.5 million deal
articles.summary: Barcelona have completed the sale of Alvaro Cortes to Royal Antwerp, bringing the defender’s five-year spell with the Catalan club to an end.The Belgian side...
articles.body:
Barcelona have completed the sale of Alvaro Cortes to Royal Antwerp, bringing the defender's five-year spell with the Catalan club to an end.

The Belgian side has reached an agreement with Barça for the transfer of the centre-back, with Barcelona set to receive €3.5 million from the deal.

The Catalan club have also protected their interests by retaining a percentage of any future sale involving Cortes.

Barcelona confirmed the agreement in an official statement: "Agreement with Royal Antwerp for the transfer of Alvaro Cortes.

"Belgian club Royal Antwerp Football Club and FC Barcelona have reached an agreement for the transfer of Álvaro Cortes.

"FC Barcelona reserve the right to a percentage of a future sale."

Cortes leaves after five years at Barcelona

Cortes joined Barcelona in the summer of 2021 after coming through the youth system at Real Zaragoza.

He initially began his career at the club with Juvenil B before spending the 2022/23 campaign on loan at CF Damm.

That temporary move gave the defender regular football in the Division de Honor.

On his return to Barça in 2023, Cortes trained during pre-season with Barça Atlètic before making his official reserve-team debut against SD Logroñés in August 2023.

The following season marked an important step in his development, as Cortes established himself permanently with Barça Atlètic and played 30 matches.

Barcelona retain a future financial interest

The €3.5m fee gives Barcelona a return from a player who developed through several levels of the club's system. At the same time, the retained percentage on a future sale leaves the door open for additional income.

Cortes also reached the first-team level during his time at the club, having made his senior Barcelona debut last season on May 13 in a La Liga meeting with Alaves.

His final season with Barça Atlètic also carried added responsibility, with Cortes serving as captain of Julian Belletti's side.

articles.standfirst: El central argentino llega procedente de Independiente y firma hasta 2030; la operación incluye el pago del 80% de sus derechos y salda la deuda pendiente por Iván Marcone
articles.summary: El central argentino llega procedente de Independiente y firma hasta 2030; la operación incluye el pago del 80% de sus derechos y salda la deuda pendiente por Iván Marcone
articles.body: El Elche ha cerrado una de las operaciones más importantes de su mercado con la incorporación de Kevin Lomónaco. Pasada la medianoche del mercado. El conjunto franjiverde ha alcanzado un acuerdo con Independiente para hacerse con el defensa argentino, que firma con el club ilicitano hasta junio de 2030. La operación se sitúa en torno a los cuatro millones de euros por el 80% de los derechos del futbolista, según ha podido saber este medio. Además, el acuerdo entre ambas entidades contempla la cancelación de la deuda que el Elche mantenía con Independiente por Iván Marcone, una operación que permite al club avanzar también en la resolución de compromisos pendientes. Lomónaco, de 24 años, se ha consolidado en los últimos años como uno de los centrales con mayor proyección del fútbol argentino. Formado en Lanús, también pasó por Platense, Red Bull Bragantino y Tigre antes de recalar en Independiente en 2024. En Avellaneda se convirtió rápidamente en una pieza importante y terminó siendo adquirido en propiedad. Ahora da el salto al fútbol español para reforzar la defensa del Elche. El argentino destaca por su intensidad, velocidad, capacidad de anticipación y contundencia en los duelos, además de mostrar personalidad para defender lejos de su área y sacar el balón jugado. Su llegada supone una apuesta importante del Elche por un central con presente y margen de crecimiento.

articles.title: Official: Barcelona confirm 20-year-old midfielder’s first-team registration; given No. 4 shirt
articles.summary: Barcelona have made a major decision on Brian Farinas’ future by officially registering the young midfielder as a first-team player for the 2026/27 season.Th...
articles.body:
Barcelona have made a major decision on Brian Farinas' future by officially registering the young midfielder as a first-team player for the 2026/27 season.

The club confirms that Farinas will wear the No. 4 shirt, which had been left vacant since Ronald Araujo moved to Liverpool on loan, after the documentation for his registration was signed on Monday afternoon and his status was updated in the league.

It is important to note that the midfielder's situation had changed dramatically during the transfer window.

In fact, Girona had advanced towards a deal that would have seen them acquire 50 per cent of his rights for around €1.5 million, but the move was stopped after Hansi Flick intervened .

Flick changes the course of Farinas' future

Flick wanted to see Farinas himself before Barcelona sanctioned his departure, and the decision proved important almost immediately.

Once the midfielder began working under the German coach, his performances in training made a strong impression .

Flick saw qualities that could potentially allow Farinas to contribute to the first team, turning a transfer that had looked increasingly likely into one that was eventually parked.

Barcelona sporting director Deco also played a role in assessing the midfielder's situation. A few weeks ago, he met with Farinas' agent to discuss the player's future.

During that meeting, Deco communicated the club's satisfaction with Farinas' development and reinforced the positive impression he had made on Flick in training.

From Girona exit to Barcelona first-team registration

The scale of the change is striking, as Farinas began the market close to joining Girona and now finds himself officially registered with Barcelona's senior squad.

That does not mean his route into the team will be straightforward, as competition for places remains intense and the midfielder understands opportunities may be limited.

What has impressed Barcelona, though, is how he has responded to the situation.

Farinas has continued working in the same manner without showing frustration or allowing the uncertainty surrounding his future to affect him.

articles.title: Ranking college football's new head coaches: Will Lane Kiffin, James Franklin, or someone else have best Year 1?
articles.summary: There are several new faces coaching across college football this season. Let's see which new head coach could have the biggest first year.
articles.body:
The 2025-26 college football coaching carousel was one of the most dramatic we've seen in some time. At the power-conference level, it was headlined by Lane Kiffin becoming one of the sport's biggest villains when he left Ole Miss for LSU in the middle of a College Football Playoff season.

Last year also saw James Franklin go from being Penn State's second-winningest coach in school history to a new face at Virginia Tech. Michigan then landed longtime Utah veteran Kyle Whittingham in a late-cycle hire.

No one has a crystal ball, of course, but the sporting world lives for predictions. With that, we try to rank all 17 of the new power-conference head coaches to find out who will make the most noise and finish their first seasons the strongest. MORE: 2026 SN Preseason All-America Team | All-America teams by decade

You are probably rolling your eyes, but Kiffin has earned this spot. The Tigers' roster is one of the most talented in the nation, featuring big-time transfer portal additions in quarterback Sam Leavitt, EDGE rusher Princewell Umanmielen and receiver Eugene Wilson III.

At Ole Miss, he won 55 games with much less talent pound-for-pound, including double-digit-win seasons in four of his six seasons there. The Tigers also benefit from a favorable schedule, getting Clemson, Texas A&M, Alabama and Texas all at home. If Kiffin makes it out of the Sept. 19 road trip to Ole Miss alive, LSU should be in for its first-ever CFP berth.

Pete Golding did one thing Ole Miss never did under Lane Kiffin: win a CFP Playoff game, and he made it look easy. The Rebels took down Tulane, SEC giant Georgia and just barely lost to Miami in the semifinals.

Thanks to one of several NCAA eligibility court case losses, he gets his star quarterback Trinidad Chambliss back, and I think Golding will be coaching with a chip on his shoulder this season, looking to prove doubters wrong. The Rebels get LSU and Georgia at home. Although Ole Miss does have to play both Texas and Oklahoma on the road, the Rebels should have no problems reaching the CFP with one or two losses. MORE: The Sporting News ranks all 138 FBS programs

Chesney won big at all three of his previous stops in James Madison Holy Cross and Ascension, featuring a combined eight postseason appearances.

The Bruins haven't reached double-digit wins since Jim Mora in 2014. With quarterback Nico Iamaleava running the Bruins' offense and a number of big-time JMU transfers coming with Chesney, UCLA is in for a quick turnaround.

James Franklin won 104 games at Penn State and took the Nittany Lions to the CFP semis just two years ago. But his 4-21 record against Top-10 AP opponents wasn't good enough in Happy Valley.

Blacksburg is the perfect place for Franklin to rebuild his coaching reputation. Virginia Tech as a program has just a 10-57 all-time record against Top-10 teams. With the Hokies, Franklin can build his program without the pressure to win everything right away.

VT does have a tough ACC slate, featuring games against Georgia Tech, Clemson, SMU and Miami. But seven or eight wins in his first season wouldn't be too shabby. MORE: Comparing the preseason AP and Coaches polls

The Wolverines have had a tumultuous offseason, to say the least. Head coach Sherrone Moore was fired in December after an investigation revealed he had an inappropriate relationship with a staffer. Michigan Athletic Director Warde Manuel is stepping down after the subsequent athletic department probe stemming from the Moore firing.

If Michigan wants fans to forget about all of that by winning football games, Whittingham is your guy. He built Utah into a consistent powerhouse, with a 177-88 record over 23 seasons, including three conference champions. He inherits a talented Michigan roster, and aside from drawing non-conference Oklahoma in Week 2 and getting both Oregon and Ohio State on the road, Michigan should do well.

Some may think Campbell should be higher on the list. But with just a single double-digit-win season with the Cyclones across his 10 seasons there, there's plenty of reason to doubt his viability in the Big Ten.

The good news for the Nittany Lions in his Year One is that Penn State doesn't have to play Ohio State or Oregon this season but does go to Michigan in Ann Arbor on Oct. 17.

Eric Morris could surprise some people in the Big 12 this year. Coming over from North Texas, he brought most of his Mean Green players from his 11-5 squad last season. The group is led by star quarterback Drew Mestemaker, who threw for 4,379 yards with 34 touchdowns and nine interceptions last year.

The Cowboys could put Oregon on upset alert early, hosting Dan Lanning in Week 2 at home. In an always-chaotic Big 12 conference race, the Cowboys play notable conference opponents in Houston, Kansas State, Texas Tech and Arizona State.

New Florida head coach Jon Sumrall has gotten plenty of buzz this offseason, and he looks to revitalize a Gator fanbase desperate to win again.

Florida's schedule is quite stiff, featuring games against Auburn, Ole Miss, Texas, Georgia and Oklahoma. But at four Troy and Tulane, Sumrall had just one season below double-digit wins, going 9-5 at Tulane in 2024.

For a program that is 29-34 over the last five seasons, it's hard to not see the Gators improve from that. Not to mention retaining running back Jaden Baugh and hiring Georgia Tech offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner were both huge for his first season.

Similar to Sumrall's situation in Gainesville, Alex Golesh comes to Auburn after a strong stint at South Florida. Across his three seasons, Golesh finished 23-15, with a 9-3 finish last year. His USF Bulls even went on the road and upset a then-ranked Florida in 2025.

Auburn hasn't had a winning season since Gus Malzahn's last season with the Tigers in 2020, so things should improve in Year One. The Tigers do have to play non-conference Baylor in Week 1 and draw Tennessee, Georgia, LSU, Ole Miss and Alabama this year.

It might not be a great record, but Auburn made a great hire in Golesh. USF transfer quarterback Byrum Brown should have a great season in the SEC, having thrown for 7,698 yards with 61 touchdowns and 19 interceptions, adding 2,265 rushing yards with 31 scores on the ground. MORE: Grading the 17 new coaching hires across the P4 conferences

Jimmy Rogers looks to replace Matt Campbell in Aimes, and he comes to the Cyclones after head coaching stints at South Dakota State and Washington State.

During his first season with the Jackrabbits in 2023, he led the program to a DI National Championship. SDSU made it to the semifinals a year later. During his lone season at Washington State last season, he went 6-6 with a win in the Potato Bowl.

But Rogers might need a season to rebuild in his first season. Iowa State lost over 40 players thanks to the Campbell departure, and he brings over a ton of guys from Washington State.

It's been over two decades since Arkansas last played for an SEC Championship. No one is truly projecting the Razorbacks to be a legitimate SEC contender in Ryan Silverfield's first season in Fayetteville. But the Hogs should at least improve. At Memphis, Silverfield compiled a 50-24 overall record, including a pair of back-to-back double-digit-win seasons in 2023 and 2024.

Arkansas hasn't done that since Bobby Petrino's last two seasons there in 2010 and 2011. Silverfield leading Arkansas to a bowl game after a 2-10 season last year would be a great improvement. That might be easier said than done, however, as the Razorbacks have to play Georgia, Texas A&M, Tennessee, South Carolina, Texas and LSU this season.

It's incredibly cool that Kansas State has one of its former quarterbacks in Collin Klein as its head coach. At just 36 years old, it wasn't too long ago that he suited up for the Wildcats, as his last season came in 2012.

Klein has been a fixture in Manhattan across two coaching staffs, joining his former head coach Bill Snyder in 2017 and staying on for now-retired K-State head coach Chris Klieman's staff through 2025. The Wildcats have gone 67-46 with Klein on staff, and his familiarity with what it takes to win there should help.

We'll have to wait and see if he learned enough from his predecessors to make some noise in the Big 12 this year.

Cal moved on from longtime head coach Justin Wilcox this offseason, and has hired Bears alumnus Tosh Lupoi as his replacement. Although this is his first head coaching gig, he has a strong coaching background, as he was on-staff with Nick Saban at Alabama from 2014-2018, and served as Oregon's defensive coordinator since 2022.

The Bears get a relatively manageable ACC slate this season, but have to play UNLV, SMU and NC State on the road.

Speaking of former Ducks assistant coaches, Oregon head coach Dan Lanning lost both his coordinators this year, as Stein was the Ducks' OC since 2023. Stein made headlines at SEC Media Days in July when he said Kentucky can win on the big stage "because of him."

We'll see how he does in Lexington in Year One, as Kentucky has a new head coach for the first time since 2013. His first season might not be pretty, as his team will play Alabama, Texas A&M, South Carolina, LSU, Oklahoma, Tennessee and Florida.

If Michigan State wants to win big again like it did under former longtime coach Mark Dantonio, it might need a coach better than someone like Fitzgerald, who went 110-101 at Northwestern.

Fitzgerald was fired from Northwestern in 2023 amid hazing allegations within the locker room, and his wrongful termination suit against the school was settled last fall.

Stanford is looking for consistency that hasn't been in Palo Alto since the first half of David Shaw's career there. Stanford general manager Andrew Luck has hired his former teammate, Tavita Pritchard, to get the Cardinal back on track.

Pritchard does not have any previous head coaching experience, but he served as a longtime Stanford assistant from 2011-2022 before spending the last two seasons with the Washington Commanders. Hiring someone who wants to build a winning culture at Stanford could turn things around. It might not be pretty in year one though, as his team will face Miami, Duke, Georgia Tech, Notre Dame, Louisville and SMU in the ACC.

It's hard to come in and start fresh after the consistent success that Kyle Whittingham brought to Salt Lake City for so long. But that's what former longtime Utes staffer Morgan Scalley is tasked with in 2026.

He played at Utah from 2001-2004, and joined Whitingham's staff as a graduate assistant in 2007. He was on staff through the entirety of Whittingham's tenure, so hopefully he learned a thing or two across his nearly two decades.

articles.title: Have title contenders done enough in transfer window to challenge Arsenal?
articles.summary: As the transfer window closes for the summer, chief football writer Phil McNulty asks if Arsenal's rivals have done enough to challenge the champions?
articles.body:
Arsenal have started the new Premier League season with two wins as the transfer window closes, looking in ominous shape to retain the crown they won for the first time in 22 years last season.

The Gunners had a quiet final day to the window having concluded their business before the traditional late rush – but those hoping to unseat the reigning champions have all been busy expensively re-shaping their squads to mount a challenge.

So how do Arsenal look? And have their main rivals done enough to prevent Mikel Arteta's side winning a second successive title?

And what are the other big issues as the Premier League's transfer business was concluded until January?

Arsenal's interest in Atletico Madrid's Argentina forward Julian Alvarez did not bear fruit, despite their attempts to persuade him away from his preferred destination of Barcelona.

Alvarez's dream move to Barcelona was emphatically blocked by the Atletico hierarchy, leaving The Gunners with hope he may take the only choice available to him to leave Diego Simeone's side.

In the end, no deal was done – and perhaps the only flaw in Arsenal's current make-up is whether they carry a consistent spearhead threat up front.

Elsewhere, they look formidable in all areas and still the team to beat after cruising past Coventry City and winning at Aston Villa in their opening two league games

They also dismantled Manchester City in The Community Shield, and have had an excellent transfer window to build on last season's success, when the Premier League was won and they reached the Champions League Final.

Bruno Guimaraes, a £75m signing from Newcastle United, showed in his brief cameo in the 1-0 win against Aston Villa what he will bring - passes that cut through the home defence and a fierce competitive edge.

England defender Ezri Konsa offers instant class in defence after moving from Aston Villa, and while Christos Tzolis had a tough night at Villa Park, substituted at half-time, he has already demonstrated what an asset he could be on the left flank.

Not quite a case of "No Alvarez No Problem", but he was hardly a deal breaker for Arsenal, who still look best equipped to win another title at the conclusion of the transfer window.

Manchester City have undergone heavy transition, from manager Pep Guardiola being replaced after 10 years by Enzo Maresca, to the departure of key figures in their glory years such as Rodri, Bernardo Silva, John Stones and Jack Grealish, as well as Savio, Omar Marmoush, Nico Gonzales, James Trafford, Nathan Ake and Tijjani Reijnders.

The burning ambition remains, however, as proved by the manner in which they have attacked the market to replenish their squad for a title tilt.

City paid £125m – equalling the British transfer record - to reunite former Chelsea manager Maresca with Enzo Fernandez, having already paid £116m to sign England midfielder Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest.

And further quality arrived in the shape of Iliman Ndiaye from Everton for £65m, the brilliant Morocco 18-year-old Ayyoub Bouaddi, who cost £85.6m from Lille, as well as Allan Elias from Palmeiras in Brazil.

It amounts to quite the rebuild, with the Fernandez deal taking City's spending to a Premier League record £458m for a single transfer window, surpassing Liverpool's £415m from last summer.

However, City have also achieved around £300m worth of player sales this summer, illustrating the vast turnover at the start of the post-Guardiola era.

An eventful window but one that leaves City, who still have so much class elsewhere, in good shape to mount a serious challenge.

Chelsea may have lost Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for £125m in the final hours of the window, but the business done this summer will still delight new manager Xabi Alonso.

Alonso opened with two Premier League wins, but goalkeeper Robert Sanchez's display in the opening victory at Fulham persuaded him to finally solve a long-standing problem by signing Emiliano Martinez from Aston Villa.

The list of incomings and outgoings are – as usual – almost too numerous to mention, but Morgan Rogers - a £117m signing from Aston Villa - has already formed a devastating trio in attack with Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro, while Maxence Lacroix is a quality defensive addition.

And in a shift in strategy, veterans Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck were brought in to add experience and their consummate professionalism to the Chelsea dressing room.

Chelsea were in the market in the final hours as well, but were bitterly disappointed when Monaco pulled the plug on their move for highly-regarded midfielder Lamine Camara as Fernandez departed.

A huge squad has no European football to offer a distraction, which is why Chelsea and Alonso could well believe they have the quality to also run close – although they remain outsiders.

Liverpool's main task this summer after appointing Andoni Iraola to replace sacked Arne Slot, was to somehow compensate for what they would miss without Mohamed Salah after he left Anfield at the end of last season.

Bradley Barcola was the prime target and eventually signed from Paris Saint-Germain for £123m. He possesses lightning pace, creativity and goals, but he is not a like-for-like replacement for Salah, preferring to operate on the left.

Victor Munoz, a member of Spain's World Cup-winning squad, is another wide man who has already shown what he can deliver with a spectacular equaliser in the 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest.

Rather than simply replace Salah, Liverpool's strategy has been to find a way to get goals from the wide positions and elsewhere rather that focus on one single player to replace the Egyptian.

All very well – but Liverpool's opening draws against Newcastle United and Forest showed a fault which holed them below the waterline last season has not been addressed.

The lack of a natural number "6" has left a midfield imbalance that leaves them horribly vulnerable to counter-attacks. Teams can still run straight through Liverpool, but Iraola showed no inclination to make a signing in that position.

Can Liverpool cure that tendency to be exposed? This could be the flaw that stops them making amends for their dismal title defence last season.

After addressing their attack last summer when they brought in Benjamin Sesko, Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha, United's window this time has been about midfield renewal as Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba were signed.

Is it enough to make United serious contenders after Michael Carrick took them to third place and back into the Champions League last season after succeeding Ruben Amorim in a caretaker capacity?

Carrick is now in permanent charge, but this has been a mixed start to the season with defeat at newly-promoted Hull City before a 5-2 win against other Premier League newcomers Ipswich Town.

United decided not to make any late moves, leaving Carrick's squad looking more like one who will realistically challenge for the top four once more but will be nowhere near the title.

Tottenham Hotspur have had a spectacular transfer window as they spent more than £300m – but results so far have been less than spectacular with two league defeats away to Brentford and at home to Newcastle United.

Roberto De Zerbi has been given huge backing, right up until the close of the window when he got his wish to bring in Mykhailo Mudryk, who played under him at Shakhtar Donetsk.

Mudryk resolved a doping case with the Football Association in July, but has not played a competitive match since November 2024.

De Zerbi must mould his host of new faces, 10 with the arrival of Tosin Adarabioyo from Chelsea, into a coherent unit, but this looks like a squad that possesses promise – with De Zerbi's biggest task getting Spurs to ditch the losing mentality that has seen them finish 17th in the last two seasons.

Aston Villa finished fourth and won the Europa League in a season of stunning success under Unai Emery, but this is effectively the start of a new era at Villa Park.

Goalkeeper Martinez, defenders Lucas Digne and Konsa, midfielders Rogers and Tielemans, as well as striker Ollie Watkins, all left.

Parma's Japan keeper Zion Suzuki replaced Martinez, while other arrivals included defenders Taylor Harwood-Bellis from Southampton, Aaron Wan-Bissaka from West Ham United on loan and Matteo Ruggeri from Atletico Madrid.

Freiburg's Swiss midfielder Johan Manzambi was another arrival, along with winger Ibrahim Mbaye from Paris Saint-Germain, striker Nicolas Jackson from Chelsea and Germany veteran Leon Goretzska.

The rebuild was fleshed out with midfielder Joao Gomes arriving from Wolverhampton Wanderers and winger Alejandro Garnacho on loan from Chelsea.

It will take even the great alchemist Emery time to fashion his new team, but he has been given the materials to work his magic for another season aiming for the top four.

articles.title: Scottish Premiership: What to look out for this midweek?
articles.summary: With five games on Wednesday and an Edinburgh derby on Thursday, plus a transfer deadline looming, what should you look out for in the Scottish Premiership this midweek?
articles.body:
Only a handful of games into the Scottish Premiership season and it could be argued that about half its team managers are already looking nervously over their shoulders.

At least most do not have to deal with a transfer deadline day before preparing for this midweek's fixtures as the domestic deadline has been delayed until the dust had settled on the five games scheduled for Wednesday evening.

However, while they have another chance to assess their reshaped squads before another hasty round of phone calls and negotiations before the transfer window closes at 17:00 BST on Thursday, Heart of Midlothian and Hibernian have no such luxury as they meet later that evening.

So what should we look out for in that big game - and the five others on Wednesday?

What are big questions in final two days of Scottish transfer window?

Why is Scotland's transfer window closing on Thursday?

Celtic sign Parma's Sorensen, with more to come before deadline

At the start of the campaign you would have imagined there would be no question marks about Martin O'Neill's position after he rescued a league and couple double out of a traumatic season in his second spell as Celtic's interim manager.

However, the veteran Northern Irishman missed last month's win over Kilmarnock after "a small medical procedure" in hospital then endured a 5-1 thrashing by LASK that meant Celtic again missed out on the riches of the Champions League.

Saturday's subsequent 2-1 home win over Falkirk was hardly convincing, adding to the doubts some supporters once again have voiced about their summer transfer dealings, and assistant Shaun Maloney was sent out to meet the media instead on Tuesday.

Neverthless, they have won all five of their games apart from that collapse in Austria and go into Wednesday's meeting with Aberdeen already two points clear at the top of the table.

Similarly, counterpart Stephen Robinson has still to convince some Dons fans despite steering them clear of relegation trouble last season then starting the season with six wins and just two losses.

To make matters worse, after Sunday's home defeat by Rangers, few will be expecting much from a trip to Celtic Park, where they have not won in 14 visits.

Indeed, Celtic won all three meetings last season after Aberdeen, who have not won in 15 away league games, edged the 2025 Scottish Cup final on penalties.

Steven Pressley was not a popular choice as Dundee head coach last season, but his subsequent charm offensive means he will be forgiven quickly for a defeat by Hibernian on Sunday that ended their six-game winning run at Dens Park.

Having admitted he failed to "find the right solutions" to thwart the Leith side, Pressley now must work out how to beat St Johnstone for the first time as a manager, having lost all three meetings with the Perth side when Falkirk manager in season 2009-10.

However, other statistics are in his favour, with St Johnstone having only won one of their latest 10 meetings and Simo Valakari's side having lost three in a row on the road after Saturday's loss to Hearts and winning just one of their latest five outings overall.

Given Saturday's 4-0 home drubbing by Dundee United, it is hard to argue that Neil McCann is not the manager most under pressure.

That came after a 5-1 thrashing by Celtic in their last home league game.

A 3-2 Ayrshire derby win over second-tier Ayr United came in between that, but that is their only victory in five outings.

McCann will take heart from two wins over St Mirren since taking charge in January, a 4-3 victory at Rugby Park in February then a 3-0 success in Paisley in May.

It leaves Kilmarnock unbeaten in four meetings with the Buddies since losing on penalties in League Cup last September after 2-2 draw in Ayrshire.

Craig McLeish's side arrive having been held to a 3-3 draw by Motherwell on Sunday after a 5-1 hammering by Rangers in the League Cup.

However, until then, St Mirren had been unbeaten in five away from home, winning the latest three without conceding a goal, and will be out to prove the Ibrox capitulation was a mere blip.

Having continued the swashbuckling style imposed successfully by Jens Berthel Askou last season, Motherwell's Alfred Johansson is probably the manager least under scrutiny.

Yet the Swede's side are without a win in four after Sunday's draw with St Mirren and are also four trips away from home without a win, albeit two of those were in Conference League qualifying against HJK Helsinki and Freiburg.

Indeed, they have lost 10 goals in their latest three outings and, including the end of last season under his predecessor, they have gone five home league games without a win.

Jim Goodwin will have had a wry smile from his hospital bed considering his United side had gone three games without scoring before crushing Kilmarnock on Saturday to end run of four without a win and three straight defeats in his absence.

They also failed to score in two defeats and one draw with Well last season, losing 2-0 twice at Fir Park - and have lost all five visits since a win in April 2023.

Goodwin will hope they can alter that trend too under assistant Sharp on Wednesday.

Rangers have only lost one of their latest five outings, but amid those results they failed to qualify for either the Europa League or the Conference League.

So Sunday's win over Aberdeen, albeit it narrow, has eased some of the pressure building early into Derek McInnes' Rangers reign.

It will be lumped back on again should they fail to beat Falkirk considering John McGlynn's side are without a win in three and have lost four of their past five at home, including their latest three in the league.

Included among those are a 5-2 hammering by Rangers on the final weekend of last season, a near repeat of the 6-3 scoreline on their previous visit, leaving the Ibrox side unbeaten in six meetings since Falkirk won 3-2 in Championship in March 2016.

Both capital clubs impressed in Conference League play-offs on Thursday, albeit Hibs ultimately lost out to two late goals at home to Gent.

David Gray's side bounced back with a 2-1 win away to Dundee that means they have suffered just one defeat in their latest seven outings.

Hearts followed up their European heroics against Rapid Vienna by holding off a spirited St Johnstone comeback on Sunday and are now unbeaten in six since a 6-1 thrashing by Benfica completed an opening four defeats under new head coach Wouter Vrancken.

A 2-1 derby victory against nine men at Easter Road in April is, nevertheless, Hearts' only win in eight league games on the road.

Should they win a third derby in a row, they will have consigned Hibs to five straight home league defeats for the first time since 2010. Some incentive!

Celtic could introduce their latest signing, Oliver Sorensen on loan from Parma, but he will surely not replace Benjamin Nygren in midfield considering the Swede scored in all three of their games against Aberdeen last season.

Two Scottish midfielders who have not quite lived up to their early promise could get their chance to revive their careers in opposition at Fir Park.

Former Dundee midfielder Lyall Cameron, whose family are United fans, could make his debut for the Tannadice side on loan from Rangers.

Meanwhile, Dylan Levitt will be keen to face his former club after his arrival from Leyton Orient.

United will also have to keep on eye on Tawanda Maswanhise, with last season's top scorer getting off the mark on Sunday and having already scored five times in six Premiership appearances against the Tannadice side, including three in his last two at Fir Park.

Former Kilmarnock defender Joe Wright could face St Johnstone after his move from Bradford City to Dundee, who might also complete the signing of Manchester United midfielder Jack Moorhouse in time to play.

Meanwhile, St Johnstone are hoping to gain permission to play former Fortuna Dusseldorf midfielder Danny Schmidt.

articles.title: Confirmed: Barcelona announce the signing of 16-year-old German prodigy for youth setup
articles.summary: Barcelona have completed the signing of German defender Mikael Baza from Hamburg SV, adding another highly rated teenager to their youth setup.The 16-year-ol...
articles.body:
Barcelona have completed the signing of German defender Mikael Baza from Hamburg SV, adding another highly rated teenager to their youth setup.

The 16-year-old centre-back has committed his future to Barça until 2029 and will initially join the club's youth B team.

Barcelona confirmed the agreement in an official statement, stating

"Agreement for the incorporation of Mikael Baza to FC Barcelona from Hamburg SV in his youth stage.

"In the signing ceremony, he was accompanied by the director of Youth Football, José Ramon Alexanco."

Baza's arrival comes after Barcelona identified the need to strengthen their options at centre-back, particularly with an eye on developing a young left-footed defender for the future.

Baza has attracted attention from several clubs despite being only 16, with his physical and technical qualities making him an appealing long-term prospect.

Understandably so, Barcelona's plan is not to rush him into senior football.

Instead, the German youngster will continue his development within the club's youth structure before any decision is made about his progression towards the first team.

His profile is particularly interesting because of his ability to operate as a left-footed centre-back, something that Barcelona have been looking for throughout the market.

Mikael Baza has signed a contract with Barcelona until 2029. (Photo by Christof Koepsel/Getty Images for DFB)

The club had already been monitoring Baza during the current transfer market. His name emerged among the candidates considered after Alvaro Cortes decided to leave Barcelona .

Hansi Flick played a role in Baza's decision

Notably, Hansi Flick has been aware of Baza for some time , partly because of his connections with Germany's youth national-team structure from his previous work as the country's senior manager.

Those links helped Flick gain a close understanding of the defender's potential.

He then intervened when Baza was considering a move to Juventus, with the German coach subsequently encouraging Barcelona to accelerate their pursuit.

That intervention appears to have helped Barça secure a player they view as a long-term investment.

articles.title: Meet the 7 underrated QBs who could be college football's next Fernando Mendoza
articles.summary: These quarterbacks are worth watching for both college football and NFL fans.
articles.body:
There might never be a better example of how drastically a quarterback class can change in a few short months than the 2025 college football season.

LaNorris Sellers, Cade Klubnik and Garrett Nussmeier were all considered legitimate first-round prospects and potential Heisman Trophy contenders. The name Fernando Mendoza was known by a much more limited number of fans, with the exception of those who stayed up deep into the night to watch him duel with Cam Ward at Cal.

The quarterbacks to watch this college football season are supposed to be Arch Manning, Dante Moore, CJ Carr, Julian Sayin, Trinidad Chambliss and Darian Mensah. It doesn't usually work out that way, though.

At least one quarterback without much name recognition in Week 1 is going to find his way into the thick of the Heisman Trophy race or the first round discussion, if not both. A rise like Mendoza's is tough to mirror, but there are a number of quarterbacks who have the talent to reach stardom in 2026.

The FCS-to-Power Four jump is a big one, but Trinidad Chambliss proved it can be done when he leapt from the Division II level. Jaden Craig could be the next to conquer it.

The Harvard transfer led a strong offense for the Crimson, throwing only 10 interceptions in 611 pass attempts over his two seasons as a starter and amassing 2,869 yards through the air last season. Craig already has a strong frame at 6-3 and knows how to protect the ball. Early reports indicate his arm strength has looked the part as he transitions to the Big 12, and he's playing an offense that worked wonders for Max Duggan and Josh Hoover.

If Craig meets or exceeds expectations at TCU, it wouldn't be a surprise to see him emerge as a legitimate NFL Draft prospect.

CJ Bailey had a couple of clunkers last season at NC State, but he showed tangible improvement from a promising freshman season and finished the year strong with three consecutive games of two touchdowns and no interceptions.

One of the nation's tallest quarterbacks at 6-6, Bailey's slight frame could be an NFL concern, but this could be the year he cleans up some of those outlier performances and emerges as one of the country's most eye-popping stars with a jump to the next level a real possibility.

No Minnesota quarterback has been drafted since 1972. That could change in 2027.

P.J. Fleck believes he has the right quarterback in Drake Lindsey, who took over for Max Brosmer in 2025 and showed promise with 18 touchdowns to six interceptions. The 6-5 Lindsey had an interception-free finish to the season, completing 66 percent of passes for eight touchdowns without a pick in his final five starts.

Lindsey just turned 21 in the weeks leading up to the season, so he could return to college football in 2027. With his size and arm strength, the right kind of season from the Arkansas-born quarterback could put him in the mix for more NFL Draft consideration than most might expect.

It wasn't long ago that DJ Lagway was considered a future NFL quarterback. It all went south for him at Florida, where he threw 14 interceptions and totaled just 2,264 yards through the air last season, but a change of scenery could bring out the talent that's in there.

Lagway just turned 21 and is heading into an offensive system that will feature him as a passer in a conference that just doesn't have as many daunting defenses. That should allow Lagway to work through mistakes, build confidence and let his natural arm talent shine through. If he can approach his potential, Lagway will have the option to either jump to the NFL or wait out a crowded class and make real money as a college senior in 2027.

Kentucky was not in a good place last season, so Cutter Boley's 12 interceptions and limited yardage totals should be taken with somewhat of a grain of salt. The 6-5 quarterback had strong showings against Tennessee, Florida and Georgia, considering the talent disadvantage around him, and he's going to a much better system with Kenny Dillingham as his head coach in Tempe.

It might be too early to talk about the NFL for Boley, but he at least has the talent to be what Sam Leavitt was at Arizona State and build confidence in the Big 12.

Including Keawe-Sagapolutele might be cheating, as he's a popular pick to be the No. 1 pick or at least a first-round pick in the 2028 NFL Draft, but he's a name worth mentioning when talking about quarterbacks who could emerge as stars in 2026.

Thrust into the starting role in a less than ideal situation as a true freshman, Keawe-Sagapolutele hit some midseason bumps year one at Cal but still threw for 3,454 yards and flashed the kind of arm talent that has NFL teams with their eye on him already.

"JKS" closed his freshman season with back-to-back games of at least 330 yards and didn't throw an interception in six of his final seven starts. With a new head coach in Tosh Lupoi, this could be the breakout season many are expecting from Keawe-Sagapolutele.

If it worked for Mendoza, it could work for Hoover, right? Indiana didn't make Mendoza, but Curt Cignetti's system certainly didn't hurt. Hoover is familiar with the style of offense OC Mike Shanahan runs, and he arrives in Bloomington with loads of experience after nearly three seasons as TCU's starter.

Hoover will have to clean up the turnovers a bit and won't have the same path to a high draft pick in part because he turns 24 next June, but it wouldn't be a surprise at all to see him post gaudy numbers at Indiana after Mendoza and Kurtis Rourke both had breakthrough years with the program.

articles.title: Roberto Gómez, durísimo con Tebas por el caso Julián: "LaLiga tenía que haber intervenido"
articles.standfirst: El periodista califica de "fracaso estrepitoso" la actuación de Laporta y Deco en el fichaje frustrado del delantero del Atlético de Madrid
articles.summary: El periodista califica de "fracaso estrepitoso" la actuación de Laporta y Deco en el fichaje frustrado del delantero del Atlético de Madrid
articles.body: Roberto Gómez fue muy crítico con Javier Tebas y LaLiga al analizar en La Tribu, junto a Javi Amaro, todo lo sucedido alrededor de Julián Álvarez y el interés del Barcelona. El periodista cuestionó que no se interviniese durante un caso que, a su juicio, ha provocado una importante crisis en el Atlético de Madrid. "Lo permite la Liga y lo permite Tebas, que por cierto lleva dos meses sin saber absolutamente nada, que está pendiente de todas las cosas y al parecer está mirando en los últimos tiempos más a favor del Barcelona que de otra cosa", aseguró Roberto Gómez. El colaborador insistió en su crítica al organismo presidido por Tebas: "Aquí tenía que haber intervenido la Liga y todo el mundo". Más allá de Tebas, Roberto Gómez fue especialmente contundente con la actuación del Barcelona durante el caso Julián Álvarez. El periodista considera la continuidad del delantero un triunfo de los dirigentes rojiblancos: "Éxito de Miguel Ángel Gil y de Enrique Cerezo, del Atlético de Madrid". En el lado contrario situó a los representantes del futbolista y al Barça. "Fracaso de los agentes, asesores que ha tenido Julián. Y, por supuesto, fracaso estrepitoso del FC Barcelona, de Joan Laporta y de Deco". Especialmente crítico se mostró con el director deportivo azulgrana. "Deco se lo tiene que hacer mirar. Esto es un petardo terrible del Barcelona, que ha asaltado sin ningún tipo de pudor la casa de un equipo que yo pensaba que eran amigos", afirmó. Roberto Gómez también reprochó al Barça que, según sus palabras, "no ha tenido el detalle en un solo momento de llamar al presidente o al consejero delegado, como muy bien hizo Florentino Pérez". El periodista aseguró que toda la situación ha afectado directamente a la estabilidad del conjunto rojiblanco: "Ha sido una vergüenza lo que ha hecho el Barcelona. Ha dinamitado. Ha metido en una crisis histórica y en un lío al Atlético de Madrid. Y eso es, aparte de estar muy mal, eso es una fechoría terrible del Barça". Según Roberto Gómez, el conjunto azulgrana mantuvo sus opciones hasta el final del mercado: "Hasta ayer el Barcelona todavía pensaba que lo podía hacer y ayer todavía insistía. Y eso es una vergüenza". Finalmente, Julián Álvarez continuará en el Atlético: "Se queda. Y esa es la gran noticia". Ahora, será turno del club rojiblanco para tratar de recuperar la normalidad: "El Atlético va a salir de esta crisis porque el Atlético se va a quedar con el jugador". Roberto Gómez cerró su análisis con otro contundente mensaje: "Lo que ha hecho el Barcelona no tiene nombre. Y espero que tome nota el Atlético de Madrid".

articles.title: Raúl Varela: "La estrella de este mercado de fichajes ha sido José Mourinho"
articles.standfirst: El presentador de La Tribu le concede "la condición de Special One de las contrataciones veraniegas"
articles.summary: El presentador de La Tribu le concede "la condición de Special One de las contrataciones veraniegas"
articles.body: El mercado de fichajes ha bajado definitivamente la persiana en Primera y Segunda División y, para Raúl Varela, hay un nombre que sobresale por encima del resto. No es el de Gordon, Hjulmand o Cucurella. Para el presentador de La Tribu, el gran fichaje del verano ha sido José Mourinho, que afronta su segunda etapa en el banquillo del Real Madrid. "Parece claro que la estrella en este mercado de fichajes, que un año más nos mantiene a una distancia sideral de la Premier, ha sido José Mourinho", afirmó Varela en La Tribu. Una elección que justificó pese a las importantes incorporaciones realizadas durante el verano: "Gordon está muy bien, Hujlmand está muy bien, Cucurella está muy bien, por citar a tres de los más llamativos y caros, pero lo que ha cambiado la película de verdad es la llegada del técnico de Setúbal al banquillo del Real Madrid". Varela considera que el contexto que se encuentra ahora Mourinho es muy distinto al de su primera llegada al Santiago Bernabéu. "Ese vestuario demanda una cosa bien distinta a cuando aterrizó con la Champions del Inter en el Bernabéu y el recuerdo de los aspersores del Camp Nou", explicó. También ha cambiado, a su juicio, el escenario en el eterno rival: "Hoy también hay un Barça dominante, pero no tanto. Flick goza de crédito y prestigio, pero no es Guardiola con su ascendencia y su corriente de believers que estiraron hasta la distorsión el viejo axioma de jugar bien, jugar bonito". El periodista recordó además cómo los éxitos europeos del Real Madrid terminaron desmontando determinados debates alrededor de la manera de alcanzar la victoria: "Se juega de muchas maneras, se gana de muchas maneras y se puede ser feliz de muchas maneras". Ahí encuentra Varela una de las principales razones para explicar el regreso del portugués. "Por eso llega de nuevo Mou. Porque el Madrid no gana y no es feliz y la paradoja reside en que el entrenador cuyo personaje más tensión metió en nuestro fútbol llega ahora en estado zen para devolver la sonrisa a este Bernabéu de turistas, luces de colores y puertas herméticas en el intento desesperado porque vuelva a sonar la música en el paseo de la Castellana". Más allá de Mourinho, Varela fue mucho menos entusiasta con el mercado realizado por los clubes españoles. "El mercado se cerró con poca chicha y menos inversión. Tiesos. Cesiones, operaciones con truco y mucha propaganda alrededor de unos futbolistas en muchos casos sin cartel que ya veremos si se amoldan al gusto del aficionado", señaló. También hizo referencia a uno de los nombres del verano: "El culebrón Julián Álvarez se resolvió demasiado pronto". Con el mercado ya cerrado, el foco pasa definitivamente al terreno de juego y a un calendario que pronto comenzará a exigir a las plantillas. "La semana que viene vuelve la Champions, la locura del domingo y el miércoles del tirón. Las rotaciones, las caritas y los primeros partidos con enjundia para nuestros grandes", advirtió. Y Varela cerró su reflexión coronando de nuevo a Mourinho como protagonista del verano: "Esperemos que estas plantillas nos deleiten, mientras tanto otorguémosle a Mou la condición de Special One de las contrataciones veraniegas. En nada ya estaremos comiendo turrones de Navidad".

articles.title: Belgian soccer club blocked by mayor from hosting Israeli opponent in Europa League
articles.summary: A Belgian mayor is refusing to let his city host Israeli club Hapoel Beer-Sheva for a Europa League game, meaning Union Saint-Gilloise will need to find a new venue for the match.
articles.body: BRUSSELS — A Belgian mayor is refusing to let his city host Israeli club Hapoel Beer-Sheva for a Europa League game, meaning Union Saint-Gilloise will need to find a new venue for the match. Union is due to host the Israeli champion on Oct. 22 after the 36-team Europa League draw was made last Friday. The Belgian league runner-up wanted to play all four of its home games in Leuven because its own stadium in Brussels does not meet UEFA standards for European competitions. The mayor of Leuven, Mohamed Ridouani, said Monday evening that the city will not grant permission for the game “for the sake of public safety,” even in an empty stadium. Ridouani said his position was consistent with not allowing Belgium’s national teams play games against Israel in Leuven. UEFA said Tuesday it had been informed about the city’s position for the Europa League game. “It’s the duty of the host club to find an alternative venue,” UEFA said of Union’s responsibility, and the stadium change “will be known in the coming days.” A UEFA ruling since the Hamas attacks on Israel in October 2023 has meant all Israeli club and national teams have played their home games in European competitions in neutral countries. Hapoel Beer-Sheva played home games in Hungary and Romania in Champions League qualifying games this season. It is rare for Israeli teams’ away games to be moved.

articles.title: Asencio condenado por conducir ebrio
articles.standfirst: Fue en agosto en Gran Canaria y dio una tasa de alcohol que casi multiplicaba por cuatro el máximo permitido
articles.summary: Fue en agosto y dio una tasa de alcohol que casi multiplicaba por cuatro el máximo permitido
articles.body: Raúl Asencio, defensa del Real Madrid, ha sido condenado por conducir ebrio en el sur de Gran Canaria hace quince días. Según adelanta 'Atlántico Hoy' el pasado 16 de agosto el futbolista (lesionado pero en pretemporada desde el 13 de julio) fue parado en un control rutinario al sur de Gran Canaria conduciendo su coche, un Porsche, en una zona de ocio (no tuvo un accidente ni conducía de forma temeraria), y dio una tasa de alcohol que casi multiplicaba por cuatro el máximo permitido, 0,90 mg/ l de alcohol, cuando la tasa máxima es de 0,25% por lo que fue condenado por cometer un delito contra la seguridad vial, (al superarse los 0,60 mg/l la infracción administrativa pasa a convertirse en un delito contra la seguridad vial). Asencio, que aceptó la pena, fue condenado tres días después, el 19 de agosto, en un juicio rápido celebrado en San Bartolomé de Tirajana. Se le impuso una multa de 14.400 euros (cuatro meses a razón de una cuota diaria de 120 euros) y la retirada del permiso de conducir durante ocho meses. En este caso, el procedimiento por el delito contra la seguridad vial quedó resuelto tras el juicio rápido. La sentencia establece una sanción económica y la privación del derecho a conducir durante el periodo fijado por el tribunal. El futbolista afrontará desde mañana y durante tres jornadas (3, 4 y 7 de septiembre) el juicio en Las Palmas de Gran Canaria junto a otros tres exjugadores de la disciplina blanca -Ferrán Ruiz, Juan Rodríguez y Andrés García-, por una acusación provisional por dos delitos de revelación de secretos, delitos contra la intimidad y, además, de un delito de distribución de pornografía infantil para los que la Fiscalía pide dos años, seis meses y un día de cárcel y una multa. El jugador no participó ni en los hechos ni en la grabación pero sí en un presunto delito de distribución de imágenes. La Fiscalía estaba abierta a retirar la acusación si el futbolista pedía perdón a las víctimas en el juicio. Las perjudicadas aceptaron ante notario esas disculpas y han cobrado las indemnizaciones correspondientes, pero no se ha podido archivar la causa contra Asencio antes del juicio, al ser semipúblico, por lo que la prueba se tiene que practicar en el plenario.
