Monga is a product of Leicester's academy and made his senior debut as a 15-year-old during the 2024-25 top-flight campaign.

He featured 30 times for the Foxes last season in the Championship before signing a five-year deal with Man City this summer.

At Leicester, Monga became the youngest goal scorer in the Championship when he netted against Preston North End in August last year.

Upon completing the signing of Monga earlier this summer, Man City director of football Hugo Viana hailed the teenager as an "exciting player" and added he has "already made huge strides in his young career".

Matos is excited to have added the teenager to his squad after the Swans continued their unbeaten start to the Championship on Tuesday night with a 2-0 win against Watford.

"He has gained plenty of experience of first-team and Championship football, and has looked confident and shown an ability to effect games at this level," said the head coach.

"We are delighted he and Manchester City have chosen Swansea as the place where they feel he can continue to develop and improve, and we are eager to see what he brings to the group."

Due to his age, Monga will require a FIFA minor application exemption before he is able to play for the Swans, who host Welsh rivals Wrexham on Saturday (20:00 BST).

Fellow wingers Ronald and Zeidane Inoussa remain with the club after moves to Millwall and Portsmouth fell through on deadline day.

articles.title: Dani Ceballos madruga para ponerse a las órdenes de Pellegrini
articles.standfirst: El utrerano aterrizó a primera hora y se marchó directo a la Ciudad Deportiva Luis del Sol
articles.summary: El utrerano aterrizó a primera hora y se marchó directo a la Ciudad Deportiva Luis del Sol
articles.body: Dani Ceballos ya es uno más en el Betis. El último fichaje del conjunto verdiblanco en el mercado, cuya llegada fue anunciada ya de madrugada, no ha querido perder ni un minuto para dar comienzo a su segunda etapa en el club. A primera hora de la mañana tomó un vuelo en Madrid y, nada más aterrizar en la capital hispalense, se dirigió directamente a la Ciudad Deportiva Luis del Sol para llegar a tiempo al entrenamiento de su nuevo equipo. El centrocampista utrerano ha participado en la sesión de trabajo de este miércoles en la que los de Pellegrini han seguido preparando el partido de Liga que disputarán el próximo viernes en La Cartuja. Un duelo muy especial para Ceballos, ya que el rival será el Real Madrid, club al que ha pertenecido los nueve últimos años, con un par de temporadas de cesión al Arsenal de por medio, y del que se desvinculó hace un par de meses pese a tener firmada una temporada más de contrato con el único objetivo de volver a casa. Ceballos ha firmado un contrato para las tres próximas temporadas, hasta el 30 de junio de 2029, y en esta primera campaña lucirá el dorsal 25, único de la plantilla que queda libre toda vez que Iker Losada, Nelson Deossa y Álvaro Fidalgo decidieron no salir en el último día de mercado pese a tener propuestas. Dani quiere ser uno más desde el primer día y convencer a Pellegrini para entrar mañana en su primera convocatoria pese a no haber realizado pretemporada (se ha ejercitado de manera individual durante todo el verano). El centrocampista utrerano, que fue padre por partida doble hace pocas semanas, será presentado oficialmente por el Betis esta misma tarde, desde las 19.30 horas en la zona 'lounge' del primer equipo en la Ciudad Deportiva Luis del Sol, junto al irlandés Troy Parrott. Con su contratación, los verdiblancos cierran un verano en el que han sumado a cinco efectivos al plantel, reforzando algunas posiciones clave, pero dejando otros puestos sin modificar por las dificultades para dar salida a jugadores.

articles.title: Liverpool's transfer window: Questions remain after summer of change
articles.summary: Feared in attack but light at the back? Liverpool have spent more than £200m in the transfer window but questions remain over whether the squad has enough depth.
articles.body:
All summer, Andoni Iraola has said that he will be "comfortable" come the start of September when the transfer window is over and he has certainty over his squad.

Senior figures at Liverpool said from the outset that this was never going to be a transfer window like last summer, when the club spent a then record £415m under Arne Slot and broke the British transfer record twice by signing Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak.

Last summer, Liverpool also made £188m from selling players such as Luis Diaz, Darwin Nunez and Jarell Quansah and ended the window with a net spend of £227m.

If you include Jeremy Jacquet (a deal confirmed in January), then Liverpool 's net spend is not hugely dissimilar this summer at just under £200m - having also signed Victor Munoz, Ronald Araujo on loan and Bradley Barcola for a combined total of £217.5m.

But they have lost senior figures with Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate all leaving for free and Curtis Jones moving to Inter Milan in a deal worth £30m. Liverpool then rejected a bid worth £80m from Manchester City for Cody Gakpo as they were unable to get a replacement.

On the basis of their first two Premier League games, there is certainly a feeling that Liverpool have left themselves short after their struggles last season.

Where concern lies is the lack of quality squad depth at the back and the absence of an out-and-out defensive midfielder but Iraola's side will end the window having made the second most expensive signing of the summer in France forward Barcola, who chose the Reds despite interest from other clubs including Arsenal .

Sources at Paris St-Germain described the Barcola deal - worth £123m - as part of the "greatest super sub window ever" after they made more than £280m in the sales of five players - including Goncalo Ramos, Lee Kang-in, Randal Kolo Muani and Ibrahim Mbaye - who often featured on the bench last season.

Despite struggling for the game time he wanted at PSG, Liverpool believe they have secured one of the most outstanding wide attacking talents in world football.

Liverpool fans could see their first glimpse of 24-year-old Barcola on Friday when Iraola's side travel to Ipswich. And there is a belief inside the club that the combined £364m trio of Wirtz, Isak and Barcola could become one of the most feared attacks in Europe.

Anfield needs some excitement after a below-par campaign last season which ultimately saw Slot lose the support of the fanbase and his job, a year after winning the Premier League.

Liverpool conceded twice in both league games so far and Iraola will be worried by how easily his side have been cut open.

Defensively, Giovanni Leoni and Conor Bradley are sidelined with long-term injuries and Joe Gomez's pre-season injury prompted Liverpool to bring in Araujo on loan from Barcelona.

The experienced Uruguayan, 27, is a stop-gap for now but Liverpool have an option to buy him for £47m next summer, when Virgil van Dijk's current contract expires.

Meanwhile, Leoni, 19, and Jacquet, 21, are viewed internally as two of the best young centre-backs in Europe. Liverpool are well stocked in that department when you include promising teenage defenders like Mor Talla Ndiaye and Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who impressed in pre-season.

The signing of 18-year-old goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans from Genk in a deal that could go up to £30m is also one for the future. Bayern Munich were also interested in the 6ft 7in Belgian and with Alisson’s contract expiring next summer and Giorgi Mamardashvili struggling to make an impact so far, Brughmans could be an option in the 2027-28 season. He is a product of the Genk academy which also developed Thibaut Courtois.

Milos Kerkez has had an underwhelming start to the campaign at left-back but the hope is that he can peak under Iraola, whom he worked with previously at Bournemouth .

On the right, Jeremie Frimpong has struggled to convince so far and Liverpool reportedly failed in an attempt to bring Malo Gusto on loan from Chelsea on deadline day.

Liverpool are willing to wait until Bradley returns from his knee injury but it is an area of worry. Araujo can also play at right-back and so can Dominik Szoboszlai, if needed.

In midfield, Iraola suggested it was not a personnel problem when Newcastle hit Liverpool on the counter twice at St James' Park.

But former Liverpool striker Daniel Sturridge, working on the game as a pundit, said that his old team has needed a defensive midfielder for three years.

Liverpool have not had a genuine number six since Fabinho left in 2023 but senior figures at the club are content with the midfield options for now.

Both Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch signed new long-term deals this year while Alexis Mac Allister, who Manchester City were interested in, is staying. Iraola will also have Wataru Endo and 19-year-old Trey Nyoni available.

The understanding is that any permanent move for a midfielder would only happen in January or next summer. Liverpool did look at Lamine Camara but there was no plan to buy a midfielder this summer.

The average age of Liverpool 's first-team signings across the past two windows is 22 and that suggests a long-term approach at Anfield. But, given their struggles in their first two games, this feels like a squad that could have done with more additions this summer.

The club's Champions League campaign begins on 10 September, meaning two games per week most of the time and that will be a new challenge for Iraola.

Liverpool believe they will be better placed once players are back from injury but only time will tell if this squad is strong enough to compete on all four fronts.

articles.title: Clemente saca la cara por Caro: "No hay dudas es de los mejores porteros de la categoría"
articles.standfirst: Para el técnico, su guardameta es, si no el mejor, uno de los mejores de la categoría
articles.summary: Para el técnico, su guardameta es, si no el mejor, uno de los mejores de la categoría
articles.body: Enrique Clemente hizo su primera aparición este curso en Girona. Quizás no fue el mejor escenario para aparecer viendo la goleada sufrida por el equipo canario. El aragonés ha sido la voz del vestuario hoy en la sala de prensa de Barranco Seco: "Hemos hablado y analizado los errores de Girona con tranquilidad, para que no vuelvan a ocurrir. No son difíciles de corregir". Errores, muchos de ellos, en salida de balón, pero para Clemente cambiar sería un error: "La mejor manera de ganar un partido es a través de la pelota, tratando de llevar lo mejor y más rápido posible a la gente de arriba. No jugamos así porque nos apetece. Es la mejor forma que tenemos para ganar, que es el objetivo del equipo", ha explicado. Muy señalado en ese partido fue el portero Caro. Clemente, que tiene una relación personal estrecha con el portero, ha sacado la cara por él: "He visto a Caro bien. No sé si hay dudas de puertas para afuera, pero dentro del vestuario ninguna. Si no es el mejor portero de la categoría, es de los mejores para mí. Caro forma parte de nuestro juego. El error no fue suyo, sino de todos. Si nos hubiésemos movido bien, hubiéramos dado soluciones para encontrar en el pase a otro jugador". El viernes Clemente y sus compañeros abrirán la jornada en el Gran Canaria ante el Leganés. El defensa amarillo ha sido cuestionado por el rival, pero sobre todo por el fichaje estrella en Segunda, Álvaro Morata: "No se esperaba el fichaje de Morata por el Leganés. Lo hemos analizado, aunque también a los otros delanteros como Soko o Millán. Es una situación especial porque la carrera de Morata ha sido brillante, espero que la siga teniendo, pero no este viernes", ha sentenciado.

articles.title: Manchester United: Have Michael Carrick's side taken a risk not signing a left-back?
articles.summary: Despite a widespread expectation they would sign a left-back this summer, Manchester United decided against - what does it mean?
articles.body:
As 23:00 BST ticked by on 1 September and the suspicion became reality, many Manchester United fans thought the same thing – what about a left-back?

Since the 2025-26 season ended, and United's summer transfer strategy started to be debated, it seemed obvious the club would move to address a perceived weakness in Michael Carrick's squad.

Luke Shaw is their only senior orthodox left-back. He started all 38 Premier League games last season, which given his previous injury record was phenomenal.

But as back-up Tyrell Malacia had unsurprisingly been allowed to leave when his contract expired at the end of June, and it is widely accepted 31-year-old Shaw will not be able to play repeatedly in a new campaign that could stretch beyond 60 games, a reinforcement was expected.

Various targets were identified, including Newcastle's Lewis Hall, Barcelona's Alejandro Balde and Racing Santander's Jorge Salinas. Finally, it came down to an attempt to get Rayan Ait-Nouri to cross the great Manchester divide by joining on loan, but City said no.

For that move to have progressed, United would have had to include an obligation to buy at a later date, but have instead chosen to bide their time for their first-choice targets.

Now the deadline has passed and, at least until the winter window opens in January, United and Carrick must stand or fall by what has to be viewed as a calculated gamble.

Man Utd fail in attempt to sign Ait-Nouri from Man City

Firstly, it must be acknowledged Manchester United really like Lewis Hall.

Had they been able to do a deal with Newcastle for him, they would have done.

However, raided by Premier League rivals for their star men this summer, it became obvious in discussions around the highly-rated 22-year-old if Newcastle were to be persuaded to strike a deal, the transfer fee would be huge.

Manchester United's summer transfer budget was finite.

Faced with the reality of the situation, they opted to maintain their focus on the 'priority' midfield area and eventually committed £70m to bring in Carlos Baleba from Brighton.

Hall, it was concluded, is someone they are prepared to wait until next summer for.

United would have been prepared to take Balde on loan. Barcelona would only sell him. Salinas had a relatively low release clause, but Atletico Madrid were favourites to sign him. By the time they moved on to Argentina defender Nicolas Tagliafico, who they missed out on anyway, United had moved on themselves.

Their decision to belatedly act on an initial approach made by an agent around Ait-Nouri was an admission they are not totally certain of the path they have chosen.

Effectively that is Shaw as first-choice left-back, with Noussair Mazraoui as back-up, in a position he admittedly plays in for Morocco, supported by Diogo Dalot, who has switched flanks before, and Harry Amass.

Right-back role for Yoro and when does Amass play?

The Amass case is a strange one. A natural left-back in United's academy, who did well in a loan spell at Sheffield Wednesday last season, then got injured straight after switching to Norwich in the winter window, Amass, 19, impressed many observers with his performances during pre-season, when he shadowed Shaw.

Yet, for some reason, United were willing to let him leave.

In the summer of 2024, then manager Erik ten Hag opted not to pick the teenager in his squad for the Community Shield, even though Amass had given a creditable account of himself up against Mo Salah in a pre-season game in the United States just a week earlier.

Ten Hag felt, physically, Amass was not at the level required. In theory, the two years that have elapsed since then should have made the defender bigger and stronger.

There have been multiple expressions of interest in Amass. Even heading into deadline day, his omission from United's Premier League 2 game against Leicester on Monday reinforced a widespread belief he would leave, probably on loan.

But that has not happened and it is not clear what his role will be within the senior squad.

The willingness to view Mazraoui as a left-back option was helped by the performances of Leny Yoro in pre-season.

Signed from Lille for £52m in 2024 as a central defender, Carrick used Yoro mainly as a right-back this summer.

Against Ipswich on Sunday, that was the slot Yoro was introduced into as a replacement for Dalot, at the same time as Mazraoui was coming on for Shaw.

At just 20, Yoro has plenty to learn about the right-back role. However, he has pace, is strong and is good on the ball. United supporters only have to look at how Josko Gvardiol has adapted to the full-back role at Manchester City after signing as a central defender to realise switching positions can have a positive outcome.

That is the calculated risk United have taken.

What they absolutely did not want to do, having taken a hardline stance all summer on the fees they were willing to pay, and a refusal to spend more than they thought a player was worth, was end up making a signing like Alex Telles, or Matteo Darmian, or Sergio Reguilon, who all arrived in recent years but were evidently short of the standard required.

It makes sense. It is probably the right call.

But that is a view taken away from the emotion of matches and the rollercoaster of results. And the reality is they will be the deciding factor in whether it was a good decision or not.

articles.title: Messi retirement and FIFA ban leave Paredes uncertain of Argentina future
articles.summary: Leandro ‌Paredes’s 10-match ban, alongside Lionel Messi’s Argentina retirement, leave former to ponder future.
articles.body:
Argentina midfielder Leandro ‌Paredes said it will be difficult to continue playing international football after receiving a 10-match suspension for his role in a brawl following the World Cup final ⁠defeat by Spain.

The 32-year-old also said Lionel Messi’s decision to retire from Argentina duty was another reason he would have to weigh up ⁠his future with the national team.

Paredes received the suspension in August, weeks after an altercation erupted at the final whistle when he shoved Spain midfielder Gavi to the ground as the ‌champions’ substitutes rushed onto the pitch to celebrate.

Paredes faced three assault charges, while teammate Nahuel Molina faced two. Both players were also fined $90,000.

“It’s going to be difficult for me to stay with the national team,” Paredes told Argentinian media on Tuesday.

“Because of the suspension as well, ⁠because of Leo’s decision … It’s going to ⁠be difficult for everything to carry on as before.

“I haven’t discussed it with the coach [Lionel Scaloni] yet, but we’ll talk about it and see ⁠what decision I make.”

Paredes said Messi’s absence from the national team would be keenly ⁠felt.

“Leo’s legacy will live on forever ⁠because of what he achieved, for never giving up and for showing that dreams are hard-won, pursued and, in the end, fulfilled …,” Paredes added.

“We’d spoken ‌in the final days of the World Cup about how the final would surely be his last match, but even ‌so, ‌we weren’t prepared for that because of what he means to us.”

Argentina return to action when they play two friendlies in September. Their opponents have not yet been confirmed by the country’s football association.

The South Americans will defend their Copa America title at the 2028 edition.

articles.title: 2026 Week 1 College Football Predictions for Every Game
articles.summary: Pack the fridge, stock the shelves and clear the couch, my friends, because Week 1 of the 2026 college football season is here.
articles.body:
Pack the fridge, stock the shelves and clear the couch, my friends, because Week 1 of the 2026 college football season is here.

The first full weekend of the campaign, as usual, is largely packed with buy games. Many preseason AP Top 25 teams are taking on a Group of Six or FCS opponent—which is a good and helpful thing for smaller programs.

But there are a few marquee matchups on the slate, too.

Saturday's slate includes Boise State at Oregon and Clemson at LSU, while Sunday features some neutral-site showdowns and Monday offers a notable ACC clash. There are important wins on the line in Week 1.

Boise State at No. 2 Oregon, Saturday, 3:30 p.m. (all times are ET)

The result of this matchup—an expected Oregon win—is less notable than getting an early opinion on Boise State's ceiling. One of the most-respected Group of Six teams this season, the Broncos could grow their bandwagon with a competitive loss to a national championship threat in a tough environment.

Clemson at No. 11 LSU, Saturday, 7:30 p.m.

Last season, LSU pulled out a relatively ugly 17-10 victory at Clemson. This year, there's a ton of excitement around LSU as new coach Lane Kiffin is set to unleash a transfer-heavy offense. The real difference-maker here, though, may actually be LSU's defense since Clemson's offense is breaking in a less-experienced group.

Wisconsin vs. No. 4 Notre Dame, Sunday, 7:30 p.m. (in Green Bay)

On paper, this shouldn't be a close game. Notre Dame is easily the more talented team. Wisconsin, however, is rightfully excited about the arrival of dual-threat QB Colton Joseph, who surpassed 2,500 passing and 1,000 rushing yards at Old Dominion last season. If the Badgers are stingy on defense as usual—aided by a raucous Lambeau Field crowd—ND could be legitimately tested.

Prediction : Notre Dame 30, Wisconsin 17

No. 24 Louisville vs. No. 9 Ole Miss, Sunday, 7:30 p.m. (in Nashville)

Within their respective conferences, Louisville and Ole Miss are solidly second-tier contenders. Barring a rout, both programs will leave Nashville with their broader expectations intact. Still, this is a valuable résumé-building win. The safer pick is Ole Miss, led by Trinidad Chambliss and a potentially explosive offense. But with Jeff Brohm on the other sideline, Louisville is fully capable of pulling the upset.

No. 19 SMU at Florida State, Monday, 7:30 p.m.

Given how Alabama and FSU's seasons diverged after last year's Week 1 upset, I promise not to overreact. Simultaneously, this is a conference game. The impact on the ACC standings could be very evident later this season, and SMU cannot afford to give away anything early. While home-field advantage matters, I'll sit in the "see it to believe it" camp for FSU's new-look offense.

Arkansas Pine-Bluff at No. 25 Missouri, 8 p.m. ET

Entering the 2025 campaign, Austin Simmons was a potential breakout star for Ole Miss. He had not played much but looked strong in limited action. Unfortunately for Simmons, an ankle injury sidelined him and allowed Chambliss to seize the spotlight. Now at Mizzou, Simmons should make a flashy debut as Missouri rolls to a comfortable win.

The short version: This should also be a lopsided game. The main storylines, though, are the official debut of new Utah coach Morgan Scalley and a first look at his revamped offense around star dual-threat Devon Dampier.

Prediction: Kennesaw State 37, West Georgia 17

No. 7 Miami at Stanford (1-0), 9 p.m. ET

Last season, Miami stumbled through a hideous first half before dominating the last 30 minutes of a 42-7 win over Stanford. So, that's at least reason to pause. But a stacked Miami team shouldn't have many issues in this early ACC tilt, especially after Stanford needed a late comeback to beat Hawaii.

Fresno State at No. 14 USC (1-0), 9 p.m.

Similar to Boise State in its trip to Oregon, Fresno State has an opportunity to earn a bit of national respect. USC isn't quite a high-end contender, but the Trojans could have a top offense behind QB Jayden Maiava. Even in a competitive loss, Fresno State can solidify itself as a Group of Six threat.

San Jose State (0-1) at Eastern Michigan (1-0), 6:30 p.m. Prediction: EMU 31, SJSU 26

Indiana State at Purdue, 7 p.m. Prediction: Purdue 45, Indiana State 14

North Carolina A&T at Georgia State, 7 p.m. Prediction: Georgia State 49, North Carolina A&T 17

UTEP at No. 10 Oklahoma, 8 p.m. Prediction: Oklahoma 52, UTEP 7

Long Island at Kansas, 8 p.m. Prediction: Kansas 48, Long Island 10

Toledo at Michigan State, 8 p.m. Prediction: MSU 30, Toledo 19

East Carolina at No. 13 Alabama, Noon ET

When these programs last met in 1998, Alabama squeaked out a 23-22 victory. If that happened again, Kalen DeBoer might get fired in the locker room. In seriousness, the spotlight will be on new Crimson Tide QB Keelon Russell, a prized prospect from the 2025 cycle who is making his first career start.

Most predictions have Texas Tech or BYU winning the Big 12. Houston is a not-so-sneaky contender, though, on the heels of a 10-3 campaign with QB Conner Weigman still leading the way. These opening two games are critical for Houston as a Week 3 showdown at Tech looms.

articles.title: Topps Unveils Champions League Debut Patches Following Massive UEFA Deal
articles.summary: Right ahead of the new Champions League season, Fanatics Collectibles and UC3 (representing UEFA and top European club teams) announced a six-year partnershi...
articles.body:
Right ahead of the new Champions League season, Fanatics Collectibles and UC3 (representing UEFA and top European club teams) announced a six-year partnership extension running from 2027 through 2033.

The deal keeps Fanatics as the exclusive maker of trading cards, stickers, and trading card games across all UEFA club competitions under the Topps brand. But for collectors, the biggest news out of the announcement is the addition of a new chase card: 1-of-1 Topps UEFA Champions League Debut Patches.

How the Champions League Debut Patches Work

The extension covers the UEFA Champions League, UEFA Women's Champions League, UEFA Europa League, UEFA Conference League, UEFA Super Cup, and UEFA Youth League.

Each Debut Patch card will feature a game-worn patch taken directly off a player's jersey during their first-ever Champions League match. After the whistle blows, Topps collects and authenticates the patch before embedding it into a 1-of-1 card.

The process fits right into a broader movement where card manufacturers are placing a heavier emphasis on patch provenance and making sure collectors get guaranteed game-worn material straight from historical moments.

The Debut Patch program will make its European club debut in the upcoming Topps UEFA Champions League Chrome Collection set landing later this season.

"Renewing our partnership with Fanatics for UEFA club competitions reflects the strength of our collaboration and our shared commitment to delivering best-in-class products for fans and collectors globally," said Aleksander Čeferin, UEFA President and Chair of the UC3 Board. "Fanatics know how to make big moments feel special. We are excited for what's next."

Bringing Debut Patches to the Champions League is in line with Fanatics' strategy to make the 1-of-1 Debut Patch the main chase card across modern sports.

What started as an MLB initiative has expanded rapidly over the past year. Fanatics has already brought the Debut Patch program to the UFC and partnered with FIFA on international soccer patches . Additionally, the holy grail of modern collecting is officially coming to the gridiron.

Topps recently announced that beginning this season, all NFL rookies will wear a Debut Patch on their jerseys. After a player makes their on-field debut, the patch will be removed and placed into a 1-of-1 autographed trading card, which will be inserted into sealed packs releasing in 2027.

Adding European club soccer and the UEFA Women's Champions League alongside these powerhouse American sports brings the concept to another massive global audience.

The long-term deal also builds on Fanatics' push into the European market, following the opening of its flagship London store last year.

"The timing of this announcement – on the eve of the Champions League season – is incredibly meaningful for us, especially as Fanatics Collectibles continues to meaningfully expand its footprint across Europe,"said Michael Rubin, Founder and CEO of Fanatics. "Together UEFA, European Football Clubs and Fanatics will continue to bring innovative products to fans and collectors for years to come – and through new introductions like the Debut Patch, bring them even closer to the players and clubs they love and support."

The partnership renewal was facilitated by Relevent Football Partners, UC3's exclusive global sales and marketing partner.

With the Champions League season getting underway, collectors can expect the first 1-of-1 game-worn UCL patches to start surfacing in Topps packs later this year.

articles.title: Expert College Football Betting Locks for 2026-27 National Champion Futures
articles.summary: Months from now, it will all make sense.
articles.body:
Months from now, it will all make sense.

After the many upsets and heartbreaks, after the many triumphs and moments of pure excellence, a single team will rule college football.

Winning a national championship is harder than it has ever been. It requires talent, and acquiring it takes mountains of cash. It demands good health and good fortune. It also requires the right coach, quarterback and schedule to make the whole thing possible.

Finding that champion is no easy assignment, especially considering how volatile the roster shuffling has become.

Despite the difficulty of the task, we are up for it.

Rather than pick one individual team and be on our way, though, we're targeting certain sectors of the odds board in search of value.

How far down the board can we go while still feeling confident in a team's championship chances? Let's find out.

Let's start with the defense, which is not something one has normally said about the Oregon Ducks over the past 15 years. Since Chip Kelly changed this program forever, however, that sentiment has been building.

Under Dan Lanning, formerly the architect of the Georgia defense, this program has found remarkable balance. Last year, the Ducks were No. 10 in scoring offense and No. 12 in scoring defense.

This year, it wouldn't be the least bit shocking to see the team finish near the top five in both categories.

It's not hyperbole to say this has the makings of the best defensive line in the country, headlined by A'Mauri Washington, Matayo Uiagalelei and Teitum Tuioti. Washington might not post the biggest numbers, but his presence in the middle is poised to make an enormous difference.

On offense, quarterback Dante Moore is the key cog, but the supporting cast is simply exceptional. Dakorien Moore, Jeremiah McClellan and Evan Stewart are terrific, and there is youth and speed up and down the depth chart.

As for the schedule, it's not easy. Road games at USC and Ohio State stand out, and home games against Michigan and Washington are noteworthy. The goal here, of course, is to make the College Football Playoff.

From there, one can only hope that recent postseason experience and an electric quarterback can do the heavy lifting.

There is so much to like about this group.

If Carson Beck didn't uncork one untimely underthrow, Miami could have upended Indiana and derailed college football's ultimate Cinderella season.

Regardless, the Hurricanes turned a corner last season in a variety of ways. And there's no reason to believe Mario Cristobal isn't capable of an encore.

Beck is off to the Cardinals, and Rueben Bain Jr., the heart and soul of the defense a season ago, is with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. A fantastic team lost some fantastic contributors, although it certainly did its part to replenish what was lost.

Miami upgraded at quarterback by bringing in former Duke QB Darian Mensah. Coming off a 35-touchdown season, he has enormous potential. He will have Malachi Toney and Cooper Barkate—his favorite target at Duke—at wide receiver.

The defense will need to fill plenty of holes, as will the offensive line. But Cristobal has become a master on the recruiting and development front, and there is no shortage of options to work with.

As for the schedule, it's underwhelming to put it mildly. A road game at Clemson could be tough, and maybe Florida State, Pitt or Duke make things weird. However, a November game at Notre Dame will be the most telling part of the season.

Last year, the team barely reached the playoff before making plenty of noise. This year, the Hurricanes must avoid the strange, outlier losses that have plagued them in the past to show they are ready for another level.

If so, they can take last year's near-triumph one gigantic leap further.

In Search of Talent and Value: Alabama (+2500)

The fact that we're using the words "value" and "Alabama" in the same general area speaks to just how far we've traveled since Nick Saban resigned.

To be clear, Kalen DeBoer has done a fine job. Following Saban was always going to be an impossible assignment, and it's been made even more difficult given the sport's uneasy landscape.

Regardless of what has happened over the last few years, Alabama is a fascinating selection at 25/1. Here's the reality with those odds. If starting quarterback Keelon Russell looks like the star many believe he can be early on, they will shrink drastically.

It doesn't matter if it comes against East Carolina or Kentucky, the sophomore QB, who has the makeup to be one of the most exciting players in the sport, will dictate what happens next.

And I think he has a chance to single-handedly change the trajectory of this program.

Sure, other pieces need to develop around him. The offensive line has to play better, and the running game needs to be a larger factor. The defense has tremendous players on the back end, although it needs retooling up front.

It's Alabama, so of course there's talent. But something seemed off for much of last year, and it has to come together now. If not, the schedule will eat the team alive.

Games against Georgia, at Tennessee, against Texas A&M and at LSU await. This team can navigate the path to reach the playoff, although it won't be easy—hence the odds.

If you believe in Russell and DeBoer, and we believe strongly in both, now is the time to get on board. After Week 1, you might never find this value again.

For Those Looking for a Potential Payday: Penn State (+8000)

When it's all said and done, Penn State will feature more than 50 new players on its roster, a product of James Franklin's departure and Matt Campbell's arrival.

If you're wondering why a team that began last season with legitimate national championship aspirations can now be had at 80/1, you can start there.

The good news is that Campbell brought with him Rocco Becht, an experienced QB who scored more than 100 touchdowns at Iowa State. He'll also have tight end Benjamin Brahmer, a 6'7" target who could have a massive senior year.

There is talent at running back. There is promise at wideout, a position that has plagued this program in recent years.

On defense, I simply love the addition of defensive coordinator D'Anton Lynn. He worked wonders at UCLA and USC, and he's poised to take his efforts to another echelon in Happy Valley.

Of all the new faces outside of Becht, Lynn could have the biggest impact in Year 1.

As for the schedule, well, it's a schedule. For a first-year head coach, it doesn't set up much better. If Penn State can beat Wisconsin at home, there's a real chance the Nittany Lions could host USC with a 5-0 record.

From there, road trips to Michigan and Washington are on tap. Those won't be easy, but the rest of the schedule is shockingly manageable. No Oregon. No Ohio State. No Indiana.

Penn State needs to make the playoff; that's step one. If the quarterback can stay healthy and the defense progresses, the Nittany Lions could work their way into the picture.

articles.title: Mercado azulgrana: más luces que sombras
articles.standfirst: Deco ha traído fichajes ilusionante, pero no pudieron llegar ni Julián ni un central
articles.summary: Deco ha traído fichajes ilusionante, pero no pudieron llegar ni Julián ni un central
articles.body: El Barcelona cerró este martes su mercado estival con buenas sensaciones. Deco ha logrado fichajes importantes que vienen a reforzar al equipo y están ilusionando al aficionado culé. Sin embargo, en el capítulo de salidas se han producido algunas situaciones que han dejado un sabor amargo. Muy productivo ha sido el capítulo de ventas, con una recaudación de más de 100 millones. En un principio, la idea de la Dirección Deportiva era el fichaje de un delantero centro y un central. Y aquí no se han cumplido las previsiones. El gran objetivo era Julián Álvarez, pero no ha sido posible ante la negativa tajante del Atlético a negociar con el Barcelona. El club azulgrana, viendo la actitud del argentino, que hizo todo lo posible por salir, le esperó hasta el último día. Y eso tuvo sus consecuencias, porque al final no pudieron ir a por otro delantero de primer nivel. Al final, el club fichó a Gabriel Jesus. Una buena oportunidad de mercado, porque es un futbolista de calidad que solamente costó 10 millones, pero que no era el gran atacante que pretendían. Eso sí, la opción Julián sigue abierta para el Barcelona de cara a próximos mercados. Tampoco llegó un central. Deco buscó uno desde el final de la temporada anterior y hubo contactos serios por Bastoni. Sin embargo, antes del comienzo del mercado, Flick paró la contratación del italiano. A mediados de agosto, Araujo salió al Liverpool y entonces volvió a abrirse la opción de reforzar el centro de la zaga. El perfil que se buscaba ya no era el mismo. La idea era fichar a un jugador joven, con proyección de futuro y sin gastar mucho dinero. Se barajaron varias opciones; Nijstad, del Twente, fue una de ellas ya que el Barça ofreció 8 millones, pero al final no hubo acuerdo y Flick se quedó sin su central. Los fichajes que ha hecho el Barça son ilusionantes. Anthony Gordon sustituyó a Marcus Rashford. El primero ya se ha ganado a la grada en los primeros partidos. Es un fichaje caro, porque ha costado 70 millones más otros 10 en variables, pero su velocidad y la intensidad que pone en el juego han sido una excelente tarjeta de presentación. También Adeyemi ha gustado. Al igual que Gordon, la velocidad es su punto fuerte y también la presión que ejerce sobre el rival. Además, no ha sido caro, porque ha costado 22 millones. La duda que presentan estos dos jugadores es si serán capaces de marcar los goles que faltan por las ausencias de Rashford, Ferran y Lewandowski. Todo hace indicar que no, así que el resto de la plantilla deberá tomar buena nota. Raphinha ya lo ha hecho, con cinco goles en tres partidos. Un fichaje que ha encantado a la culerada es el de Rodri. Un futbolista que encaja a la perfección con el estilo Barça. Además, se lo han levantado al Real Madrid, un factor que no es baladí. Puede que no fuera un futbolista tan necesario, porque en la medular el Barcelona tiene efectivos de sobra, pero aportará mucho en el juego y en liderazgo. No ha sido una incorporación barata: 60 millones fijos y 15 en variables. Las llegadas de Livakovic y Cancelo, aunque este último ya estuvo cedido el pasado ejercicio, también son buenas noticias. El primero da mucha solidez a la portería, mientras que el portugués ofrece muchas alternativas en el lateral. Las ventas han sido otro capítulo destacable. El club ha ingresado algo más de 100 millones. Destacan los 50 de Ferran Torres, que quiso irse al PSG; los 11 por Ansu Fati; otro tanto por Tommy Marqués, y 8,5 por Héctor Fort. El resto viene de las ventas de jugadores del filial. Una labor de mucho trabajo que hay que reconocer a Deco. La desilusión ha venido en las salidas. Sobre todo, por Casadó. El club quiso venderlo por 25 millones, pero al final no llegaron ofertas y solamente salió cedido en el último instante al Dépor, sin dejar nada en caja. Tampoco salió Balde, por el que el Barcelona podría haber ingresado unos 40 millones, que era su precio de mercado. Hubo ofertas de cesión que no interesaban al club.

articles.title: Sam Johnstone: Goalkeeper joins Celtic on loan from Wolves
articles.summary: Former England goalkeeper Sam Johnstone joins Celtic on a season-long loan from Wolverhampton Wanderers.
articles.body:
Former England goalkeeper Sam Johnstone has joined Celtic on a season-long loan from Wolverhampton Wanderers.

The 33-year-old will provide competition for Finland international Viljami Sinisalo at the Scottish champions.

Johnstone, who won the last of his four caps in 2023, made 17 appearances last season but lost his Premier League starting place at relegated Wolves in December and has not played since an FA Cup loss to Liverpool in early March.

"I'm buzzing to be here and I'm excited to get going," said the goalkeeper, who began his career at Manchester United and has had spells at Aston Villa, West Bromwich Albion and Crystal Palce.

Talking to club media, he added: "I didn't need convincing by anyone, but Joe Hart rang me the other day just to reiterate what a place this is, what a great group of lads and how the fans are unbelievable.

"You hear about the size of the club, and you know about the size of the club, but just being here for a day, you notice how big the club is.

"And the pressure to win, which is what I like – pressure to win, pressure to perform and we all want to win trophies.

"I think everyone knows the goalie groups are a tight-knit group. We work closely together every day and hopefully I can help Vil and he can help me, and we push each other and we support each other along with the other goalies and the goalie coaches."

Kasper Schmeichel had been first choice at Celtic since the summer of 2024, but played his last game in February and subsequently retired due to a shoulder injury.

"He is a quality keeper with excellent experience at the highest level," said manager Martin O'Neill said of Johnstone. "I think he will be a very good addition to our goalkeeping team."

articles.title: Lincoln Riley Responds to USC Attendance Criticism After CFB Opener at Coliseum vs. San Jose State
articles.summary: USC coach Lincoln Riley brushed aside the conversations sparked by the attendance for the Trojans' 42-26 victory over San Jose State to open the 2026 college football season.
articles.body:
USC coach Lincoln Riley brushed aside the conversations sparked by the attendance for the Trojans' 42-26 victory over San Jose State to open the 2026 college football season.

"This is USC — people are going to have an opinion," he said Tuesday, per ESPN's Paolo Uggetti . "I don't buy into the false narrative. I think that comes from a lot of people that don't follow our program, and most of those have never stepped foot in the Coliseum."

The official attendance for the game was listed at 51,144, though the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum looked far emptier as the event kicked off.

While Riley contends this is a "false narrative," USC felt the need to issue a statement addressing the situation.

"We understand the factors that impacted Saturday's attendance," the school said, per USA Today 's Jordan Mendoza . "We have high expectations and a premier home schedule this season, and we know the competitive advantage an electric Coliseum atmosphere can provide our program. We thank our fans who showed up Saturday and look forward to seeing increased attendance the rest of the season."

The extreme heat in Los Angeles may have dissuaded fans from showing up, and a Week 0 clash against San Jose State isn't a major draw in the best of conditions.

For some, though, the images of empty seats at the Coliseum reflected a general lack of excitement around the program.

USC has yet to reach the College Football Playoff since hiring Riley ahead of the 2022 campaign. In addition, the heyday of the Pete Carroll era gets further and further away with each passing year.

The Trojans sat 14th in the preseason AP Top 25 and Coaches Poll, so they're firmly in the playoff discussion. But the fans have spent roughly a decade — maybe more — buying into the hype, only to wind up disappointed with the team's finish.

Nothing gets people on board like winning, and USC has big home matchups with No. 2 Oregon, No. 17 Washington and No. 1 Ohio State on the schedule. The attendance will inevitably climb.

But the relatively small crowd last week isn't something the school should write off given the larger context.

articles.title: Champions League Players to Wear 'Debut' Patches for 2026 Season, Will Be Used for Trading Cards
articles.summary: Following in the footsteps of other major sports leagues, the UEFA Champions League will incorporate debut patches on the jerseys of debuting players during 2026-27 Champions League play.
articles.body:
Following in the footsteps of other major sports leagues, the UEFA Champions League will incorporate debut patches on the jerseys of debuting players during 2026-27 Champions League play.

According to David Ornstein of The Athletic, the patches are a result of a deal between UEFA and Fanatics, and they will be used to create ultra-rare and desirable Topps trading cards.

The debut patch cards have been a major hit in other sports leagues, including MLB, NBA, WWE, UFC and Formula 1.

Topps already forayed into soccer before with MLS debut patch cards, and the program is also coming to the German Bundesliga and the FIFA World Cup, as well as the NFL.

Champions League debutants will wear the debut patches, which will incorporate the UCL's "starball" logo. Only players who actually appear in matches will qualify to have their patches taken and put into cards.

Topps' debut patch cards have become among the most highly sought after cards in the entire hobby due to their scarcity, as every debut patch card is a one-of-one, complete with the game-worn patch and an autograph.

Pittsburgh Pirates ace starting pitcher Paul Skenes' debut patch card sold for $1.1 million last year, and Dallas Mavericks star and reigning NBA Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg will see his debut patch card go up for auction soon.

Topps is expected to be able to obtain the debut patches and begin work on the cards for the UEFA Champions League during the 2026-27 campaign, per Ornstein, while the Women's Champions League is expected to follow in 2027-28.

articles.title: Valencia rescata el mural de la selección española que fue vandalizado en Barcelona
articles.standfirst: El artista Alberto León volverá a pintar en la capital del Turia la obra dedicada al título mundial de España, destruida apenas 24 horas después de su estreno en la ciudad condal
articles.summary: El artista Alberto León volverá a pintar en Monteolivete la obra dedicada al título mundial de España, destruida apenas 24 horas después de su estreno en la ciudad condal
articles.body: Valencia dará una segunda vida al mural dedicado a la selección española de fútbol que fue vandalizado en Barcelona apenas un día después de su creación. El artista tinerfeño Alberto León volverá a ejecutar la obra, esta vez en la fachada del Centro Municipal de Actividades para Personas Mayores de Monteolivet, en una intervención promovida por el Ayuntamiento de Valencia. Los trabajos comenzarán este jueves en la plaza Vicente Alcober Coloma y supondrán la recuperación de una pieza que había alcanzado notoriedad tras ser destruida a las pocas horas de su inauguración en Barcelona. El mural representa al seleccionador nacional, Luis de la Fuente, levantando la Copa del Mundo mientras es manteado por sus jugadores tras la victoria final ante Argentina. La iniciativa surgió después de que el consistorio valenciano contactara con el artista para ofrecerle una alternativa tras la desaparición de la obra original. La nueva versión contará con una superficie de mayores dimensiones y mejoras técnicas orientadas a garantizar una mayor conservación, apuntan fuentes muncipales. Desde el Ayuntamiento consideran que la actuación supone tanto un homenaje a los éxitos recientes de la selección como una muestra de apoyo al arte urbano y a sus creadores. La concejala de Turismo y presidenta de la Junta Municipal de Russafa, Paula Llobet, destacó que la ciudad ha querido brindar un espacio permanente a una obra cuya exhibición en Barcelona tuvo una vida efímera debido a los actos vandálicos: “Nos parecía una magnífica oportunidad que Alberto León pudiera volver a realizar en Valencia una obra que tuvo una vida tan corta en otras calles. Aquí tendrá un espacio mucho mayor, podrá mejorar su técnica y, sobre todo, permanecerá para que los vecinos y visitantes puedan disfrutar de ella con total respeto y orgullo por nuestra selección", detallaba la concejala. El mural se ubicará en el barrio de Monteolivet, donde pasará a formar parte del patrimonio artístico urbano del distrito. Además de recuperar una creación que había quedado truncada, la actuación permitirá exhibirla en un formato de mayor escala que el concebido inicialmente.

articles.title: Trabzonspor: Turkish club accept Fatih Tekke's resignation following Europa League exit
articles.summary: The Turkish club accepts the "emotional" resignation of head coach Fatih Tekke after initially rejecting his request to step down.
articles.body:
Trabzonspor have accepted the "emotional" resignation of head coach Fatih Tekke after the Turkish side initially rejected his request to step down.

Tekke, who led Trabzonspor to a third‑place finish in the league last season, tendered his resignation after his side were knocked out of the Europa League play‑off round 5‑0 on aggregate by Hungarian club Ferencvaros.

After rejecting his request on Friday and suggesting the 48‑year‑old made the decision under the "intense emotional impact" of the Europa League exit, the Super Lig club have now agreed to part ways with their head coach.

In a statement released on Wednesday, Trabzonspor said it reached a "mutual understanding" with Tekke and decided to part ways "in line with Trabzonspor's interests and long‑term objectives".

The statement added: "Over his approximately 18‑month tenure, Fatih Tekke brought significant value to Trabzonspor.

"Beyond contributing to the development of the players added to our squad during this period, he delivered important sporting and financial gains for our club. By bringing the Turkish Cup back to our museum, he once again wrote his name into Trabzonspor's history.

"At this point, we reached a mutual understanding with our coach - who stated he would never allow his presence to harm Trabzonspor in any way - that drawing a new roadmap, prioritising the club's interests above all else, had become unavoidable.

"We thank our coach for his efforts, his dedicated work, the successes he delivered, and the value he added to Trabzonspor."

Trabzonspor reject manager's 'emotional' resignation

Trabzonspor, who signed Mohamed Salah in the summer, will still play European football this season, in the Europa Conference League, with Scottish side Hearts among their six opponents.

The seven-time Turkish champions also signed Liverpool's Premier League winner Fabinho in the summer while goalkeeper Andre Onana has also rejoined the club on loan from Manchester United.

Salah, 34, made the shock decision to sign for Trabzonspor last month after mutually agreeing to end his contract at Liverpool last season.

The Egypt international is the third-highest scorer in the Reds' history, behind only Ian Rush and Roger Hunt, after scoring 257 goals in 442 appearances following his move from Roma in 2017.

Salah scored his first two goals for his new club in Saturday's 2-1 win against Istanbul Basaksehir.

articles.title: Nicolas Kuhn lands Bundesliga move after falling out of favour following £17m Celtic transfer
articles.summary: Former Celtic winger Nicolas Kuhn has returned to Germany after completing a season-long loan move to Borussia Monchengladbach from Como.The 26-year-old head...
articles.body:
Former Celtic winger Nicolas Kuhn has returned to Germany after completing a season-long loan move to Borussia Monchengladbach from Como.

The 26-year-old heads to the Bundesliga just over a year after Celtic banked around £17million from his move to the Serie A side.

Kuhn enjoyed a successful spell at Parkhead following his arrival from Rapid Vienna, with his performances for the Hoops earning him a lucrative switch to ambitious Como.

However, the German struggled to establish himself under Cesc Fabregas in Italy, making just six league starts and registering one goal and one assist.

Kuhn was then left out of Como's squads at the beginning of this season, paving the way for his return to his homeland with Borussia Monchengladbach.

"It has always been my goal to play in the Bundesliga and I am very happy that it is now going to become a reality," Kuhn said.

Gladbach sporting director Rouven Schroder believes the former Celtic attacker will add several qualities to their forward line.

"Nicolas is left-footed, versatile in attack, fast, can solve one-on-one situations, and is also dangerous in front of goal.

"He has proven all of this in his career, not least on the European football stage."

articles.title: Claudio Braga: Coach 'bets' on striker staying on at Hearts
articles.summary: Head coach Wouter Vrancken would wager on Claudio Braga remaining at Hearts and thinks a second full season at Tynecastle can enhance the striker's chances of a big move.
articles.body:
Head coach Wouter Vrancken would wager on Claudio Braga remaining at Hearts and thinks a second full season at Tynecastle can enhance the striker's chances of a big move.

"He is fully focused here, fully committed," said the Belgian of the 26-year-old.

When asked if the Portuguese would still be at the club when the transfer window closes on Thursday, Vrancken added with a chuckle: "I think he will be here. I'll bet on this.

"But you never know, so let's hope that we can keep him because he has a lot of value for the team."

Braga has scored twice and provided three assists in 10 outings this term while he hit the net 17 times during his first campaign in Edinburgh, having been signed from the Norwegian second tier.

"He's important because he has quality," said Vranken. "He is also coachable and thinks about the team. He has the mindset that the team is the most important thing. For me, that's an extra reason to want to keep him.

"It can be a good thing for him to stay and show himself in a different style of play because the bigger teams are not looking for a player who does one good year in a certain style of play.

"I think when you can show yourself, that it's not a lucky shot, he is consistent in quality and he can show himself in different ways of playing and in different positions, then it adds to his personality or to his abilities as a player and I think the range of [interested] clubs will be bigger."

It has been a busy summer of change for Hearts, with Vranken replacing Derek McInnes and 14 new signings to compensate for 12 departures.

"I would never say settled because I know what can happen in the last seconds of such a window," said the head coach of any late transfer activity before Thursday's derby with Hibernian at Easter Road.

"We are discussing possibilities all the time, incoming, outgoing."

articles.title: Mbappé, objetivo de secuestro de una banda, junto a raperos y ejecutivos
articles.standfirst: Detenido Lester Z, de 18 años, cerebro de una peligrosa banda francesa
articles.summary: Detenido Lester Z, de 18 años, cerebro de una peligrosa banda francesa
articles.body: El delantero del Real Madrid, Kylian Mbappé, figuraba como uno de los objetivos principales en la lista de la peligrosa banda francesa liderada por un joven de 18 años bajo el seudónimo de Lester Z. Lo cuenta el prestigioso diario 'Le Parisien' En realidad se trata de Clément L., de 18 años, franco suizo y ya encarcelado por robo a mano armada y proxenetismo, momento en el que se ha descubierto que planeaba secuestrar a 26 personas: futbolistas, raperos y empresarios adinerados. Fue identificado tras el asalto a un relojero el pasado abril en Neuilly-sur-Seine. Desde su celda en la penitenciaría de Villepinte (Seine-Saint-Denis), este joven daba órdenes por Snapchat usando el seudónimo "Lester Z". De sus dos teléfonos se extrajeron las direcciones de cantantes, futbolistas y empresarios, todos ellos con una gran fortuna. Entre ellos se encuentran un mayorista chino en el distrito 19, joyeros y un mayorista turco de carne en Val-d'Oise, cuya fortuna se estima en millones. Y un objetivo incomparablemente más rico: "También quería atacar a un rapero y al futbolista Kylian Mbappé", añade una fuente judicial. Al ser interrogado, el joven, que bandonó la escuela en su primer año de formación profesional en cocina, asegura que aspira a retomar sus estudios y convertirse en chef.

articles.title: Matarazzo: "Estoy contento con los fichajes de Fort y Sarr y el equipo que tengo"
articles.standfirst: El técnico, que mañana no podrá estar en el banquillo por su expulsión ante el Espanyol, tiene claro que sus ayudantes le sustituirán bien ante un Celta complicado
articles.summary: El técnico, que mañana no podrá estar en el banquillo por su expulsión ante el Espanyol, tiene claro que sus ayudantes le sustituirán bien ante un Celta complicado
articles.body: Pellegrino Matarazzo ha mostrado su satisfacción con los fichajes de Mamadou Sarr y Héctor Fort, así como con las salidas que se han producido, con las que espera que su Real Sociedad haga una gran temporada. El técnico de Nueva Jersey espera mañana en Anoeta a un Celta complicado por sus diferentes formas de jugar. La primera pregunta a Matarazzo en su rueda de prensa es si cree que la plantilla que tiene para esta temporada es mejor que la que tuvo en la pasada. “Es difícil decir eso ahora, pero creo que tenemos potencial y que lo importante no es como estemos ahora, sino donde estamos el 26 de mayo, cuando termine la temporada. El proceso, el desarrollo, son muy importantes”. Matarazzo ha sonreído y mucho cuando le han preguntado si le han fichado todos los futbolistas que pidió, quizás porque esperaba alguno más o porque alguno de los que han llegado no es exactamente el que aguardaba. “Creo que hemos hecho un buen trabajo con la llegada para el centro de la defensa de Mamadou, un jugador rápido, que cubre espacios grandes y ganador de duelos, y de Héctor para el lateral derecho, porque es un perfil diferente a Aramburu, que es un fantástico defensor, Héctor igual es más vertical y hábil. Estoy contento con los jugadores fichados y con el equipo que tengo”. ¿Están las dos caras nuevas para jugar ya? “Están en la convocatoria porque es importante que de adapten lo antes posible, tenemos muchos partidos en pocos días, sin apenas entrenamientos, luego ya veremos mañana si les veis sobre el césped”. La Real tenía un problema defensivo, como lo prueba que fue el equipo más goleado en la pasada Liga, y ha fichado dos defensas, así que parece que se puede solucionar o, al menos, reducir ese mal. “Defender tiene muchas aristas y estamos trabajando en todas”. Matarazzo ha sido cuestionado por algunos de los nombres propios de los que horas antes había hablado el director de fútbol Erik Bretos, explicando por ejemplo la salida a última hora de Mikel Goti. “Goti es un jugador muy talentoso, pero sólo puede jugar en una posición. En mitad de la pretemporada tuvimos buenas conversaciones, también tuvo alguna molestia que le impidió poder estar a tope. Creo que tiene talento, pero con pocas opciones aquí para estar en el campo, porque aquí tenemos muchos jugadores que pueden jugar en su posición y lo que necesita es jugar, así que creo que su salida es buena para su futuro”. Pacheco sí que ha decidido quedarse en la plantilla, pese a que se ha quedado fuera de las dos primeras convocatorias. “Sí, hablé con él y nunca le he dicho que se tuviera que ir, tampoco fue un mensaje el no meterle en la convocatoria, pero tiene que hacer más, ser más ambicioso, se lo he vuelto a decir esta semana, si quiere jugar tiene que enseñar su potencial en los entrenamientos, y creo que ha tenido una buena reacción a esas palabras que tuvimos”. Zakharyan también sigue, pero sin protagonismo. “Ha hecho una buena pretemporada, he visto lo mejor de él desde que estoy aquí. Hemos hablado y le he dicho que tiene que ser paciente, trabajar bien. Entiendo que los jugadores quieren estar en el campo y que se enfadan si no lo hacen, el otro día mostró sus sensaciones, hemos hablado y tiene que ser paciente y, cuando llegue su oportunidad, aprovecharla”. Matarazzo ha dicho como va a vivir el partido de mañana estando sancionado. “Estaré en el campo, en algún palco del campo. No estoy contento con la tarjera roja del otro día, espero que sea la última. Y siempre se nota el carácter de John, es un gran tipo, con mucha energía, me encanta tenerle en el staff y creo que entre él y el resto de ayudantes lo van a hacer muy bien”. Es evidente que había del Celta. “La pasada temporada vimos que utilizó hasta tres distintas estructuras para salir con el balón jugado, así que tenemos que estar preparado para sus estructuras. Esperamos una cosa, vamos a ver si la encontramos”.
